item.content:encoded: Cameron Balser running Credit: Alessandro Portante NEED TO KNOW Cameron Balser broke the Trans America Run record, running 3,000 miles in 41 days across 12 states Balser faced physical, mental, and safety challenges, including traffic dangers and running up to 16 hours daily He credits his support team and community for helping him achieve his goal and inspire others through his journey After 41 days and over 3,000 miles, ultramarathoner Cameron Balser reached New York City Hall to set a new record for the Trans America Run on Friday, Nov. 20. Eight years in the making, Balser, 35, hoped to beat the previous record set by Pete Kostelnick, who ran from San Francisco City Hall to N.Y.C. in 42 days in 2016. The determined athlete was able to do so, beating Kostelnick by 13 hours and 45 minutes. Following the feat, Balser, 35, opened up to PEOPLE about what the run means to him, what some of the hardest parts were and how he leaned on Kostelnick to keep himself grounded in why he wanted to take this on in the first place. “Running’s always been something I’ve been very passionate about. I just didn’t know where that was gonna go. I ran some more ultramarathons and I met Pete, who had the record, and got to talk to him about his trip across the country,” Balser says. “That influenced me to want to run around America. In 2023, I ran the perimeter of the United States. I did a solo thing and I ran 11,170 miles in 294 days around America. After that, it kinda gave me a good resume for people to wanna kinda back me.” Cameron Balser running across America Credit: Alessandro Portante For the Trans America Run, Balser was sponsored by Mount to Coast . He started his race in San Francisco on Saturday, Oct. 10 before crossing 12 states over 41 consecutive days, climbing more than 42,000 meters and averaging 72.1 miles per day. Some days, he spent up to 16 hours running. “The team would wake me up around 4:25, 4:30. I would wake up then and have 10 minutes to slam some food and try to wake myself up. By 5:00 a.m. almost every day, we would start running,” Balser says. Every five miles, he says he would “eat literally as much as I could.” “Then I would go back out there and the team would be looking for anything that would need water, food and stuff like that. Running from 5:00 a.m. to basically 9:00 p.m. every night and then 10 minutes I would have a little bit of a wind down and then I would go to sleep and I did that for basically 41 days straight,” Balser reflects. Prior to the run, Balser worked on a regenerative farm and got used to the long hours. After the farm work, he would run 25 to 30 miles a week, and then on weekends would run 40 to 50 miles. “I was more prepared than I thought. We were very lucky and fortunate that it literally felt like miracle after miracle was unfolding in front of us,” Balser says. Balser says the most surprising aspect was spending up to 16 hours every day with himself, with him reaching a moment where he felt like he had “nothing else to give.” However, what changed his mindset was when his friend, Sam, told him to “let the love in.” “That moment after that it felt like everything was unfolding more than I could imagine. It was like I was keeping something. I had a little bit more to let go, and it was a big thing to let go, and I can just feel that energy of love, and that’s what was most important about this trip was showing how good it is to love yourself with the people around you and follow what you’re truly passionate about,” Balser says. Cameron Balser and a group running at night Credit: Alessandro Portante Along the route, people would join him and run segments with him. “We had the people we needed at the right place at the right time. We had teammates, fly in and come and help us as well. Whatever time they had to give, they gave,” he says. “As we got to Illinois, Indiana, Ohio, all the way to New York City, I hardly ran any days alone. I had a few days in Pennsylvania, but there was always somebody coming out, especially if they’re local, they were telling us everything about their city and how happy they were, and proud they were of the city,” Balser recalls. The biggest challenge about the run, however, was “myself,” he says.“Everything else was taken care of. I wrote down a lot of things I wanted for the trip, and everything I ever could have dreamed of was right in front of me. I was like, ‘Dude, there’s nothing you have to worry about other than running.’ ” Then, whenever he had a low moment and he found himself fighting with his own ego, “I was just like, ‘What do people think of me if I can’t run, if I have to walk this in?’ ” he says, noting that his team supported him and let him know that if he had to walk it in, that’s what they would do. The other challenge that he faced was traffic. Balser, who wore a safety vest during his trek, says that “75% of the time” he was “watching for cars, and someone on their phone or just not paying attention.” “I encountered almost dying every day, so that was a lot. I was focused on the next step I was taking and trying to be as present as I could be. I lost my vision day by day and I had nothing more I could focus on rather than what was in front of me or I would get myself in a position where I was looking too far ahead or looking back too much,” Balser says. Cameron Balser and his van Credit: Alessandro Portante Not only that, but Balser had to put on music or listen to a show on Netflix to drown out the noise of the passing cars — all while he tried to maintain his safety. “There was a good portion where, when the traffic was insane, I had to drown that out, which as crazy as it sounds, if I didn’t, I felt like I could have PTSD from just hearing cars go past me at 75 miles per hour in the middle of Nebraska or Iowa,” he says. He notes, “I listened to everything you could think of, and I thought of every thought you could think of, probably a thousand times until my brain would go dead. I knew if you can’t see them, they can’t see you.” Helping to keep him safe was his team, a support crew following him in a van, who sometimes would have people run with him. He also credits the people who cheered him along the way. Cameron Balser in New York City Credit: Alessandro Portante Every day, he would try to get about six hours of sleep, and that’s where most of his recovery would come from. If there was a hotel within five miles of where he stopped running, he and his team would stay there. Most of the time, however, they slept in the van. When Balser had completed his run, he didn’t expect to be greeted by such a large crowd of people. “I felt like this is really what the world is about and this is the world I wanna live in. I saw so many smiling faces and I stayed after and hugged everybody that came out there,” he says. “It’s something I’ll never forget and I will always know if you put everything into a day or into your life, there’s nothing you can’t do. I’m just gonna love this experience more and more and more and more. Whatever I can do to help other people, that’s what I’m gonna do, I’m just grateful,” Balser continues. Never miss a story — sign up for PEOPLE’s free daily newsletter to stay up-to-date on the best of what PEOPLE has to offer, from celebrity news to compelling human interest stories. Now that the run is finished, Balser is focusing on recovery and continues to give himself the love that he needs. He hopes to inspire people with his story, saying, “I’m glad to show people if you go out there and it’s something that really aligns with you and it’s not anything out of ego and it’s just out of love, like, there’s really nothing you can’t do.” While he was the person physically running, he says, “I couldn’t have done it without everybody.” Balser adds, “Without people praying for me and people along the way that came out and helped us with certain things, doing laundry or getting us food. item.title: Luka Doncic accuses courtside fan of pushing him during heated wristband incident
item.description: Luka Doncic accuses courtside fan of pushing him during heated wristband incident originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Luka Doncic had a rough Friday night in San Antonio. The Los Angeles Lakers lost 99-96 to the San Antonio Spurs , dropping their season record to 15-4. The loss also knocked Los Angeles out of the NBA Cup. Things got even worse for Doncic after the final buzzer. As he walked toward the tunnel at the Frost Bank Center, he got into an argument with a fan sitting near the walkway. Video from the arena showed Doncic tossing his wristband to a female fan. A moment later, he heard she did not want it. Doncic walked back to pick it up and the man sitting next to her returned it before shoving the Slovenian star in the back. Doncic turned around right away to confront the man. Lakers forward Jarred Vanderbilt and arena security quickly stepped in to separate them. After the game, Doncic spoke to reporters about what happened. He blamed the fan for starting the physical contact. "I just threw my wristband like I do almost every game, and then I heard she didn't want it, so I went back to grab it, and he just pushed me, and then I gave it to somebody else," Doncic said . Luka Doncic on the altercation with a fan: "I just threw my wristband like I do almost every game, and then I heard she didn't want it, so I went back to grab it, and he just pushed me, and then I gave it to somebody else." https://t.co/aCfOCG7iEt — BrickCenter (@BrickCenter_) November 28, 2026 Many fans on social media did not believe his side of the story. Several users noted that the video made it look like Doncic threw the band out of anger after a tough loss. Los Angeles controlled the game early on. The Lakers built a 20-point lead in the first half and went into halftime ahead 54-38. Everything changed in the third quarter. San Antonio outscored Los Angeles 30-14 to get right back into the game. Doncic played 39 minutes and finished with 31 points, eight assists, six rebounds, and three steals. He struggled badly from deep, making just 1 of his 13 shots from 3-point range. Austin Reaves added 21 points for the Lakers, and Walker Kessler finished with 10 points and 13 rebounds. Stephon Castle led the Spurs with 26 points. Victor Wembanyama added 25 points and 16 rebounds to help San Antonio complete the comeback. item.title: Serie A Liveblog: Inter-Genoa, Torino-Lazio and Frosinone-Parma
item.description: Serie A Liveblog: Inter-Genoa, Torino-Lazio and Frosinone-Parma Join us for all the build-up and action as it happens from today’s three Serie A games: Frosinone-Parma, Torino-Lazio and Inter-Genoa. We begin at 15:00 CET [14:00 GMT] with Frosinone hosting strugglers Parma at the Stadio Stirpe. The Ciociari sit in seventh in a European spot, but have lost their last two league matches. Parma, meanwhile, travel to Frosinone after a 5-1 loss to Roma last weekend. The Ducali, coached by Italy 2006 World Cup winner Alberto Gilardino, have lost three of their last five games, including the last two, and have eight points. Serie A leaders Lazio visit Torino at 18:00 CET [17:00 GMT] in a reunion between former Milan players Gennaro Gattuso and Ignazio Abate. Gattuso also coached Abate at San Siro. Lazio are the only unbeaten team in Serie A this season alongside city rivals Roma, but will play Torino without the injured Kenneth Taylor. Inter-Genoa ends today’s Serie A program at 20:45 CET. The Nerazzurri and the Grifone will meet again next Tuesday, also at San Siro, in the Coppa Italia Round of 16.

item.title: LIVE NOW: Pride of Detroit Movember marathon stream with special guests
item.description: THIS SATURDAY , our Movember drive winds down with its biggest event of the month: our 16-hour live stream full of Detroit Lions talk, guests, and a bunch of shenanigans. We’ve got the live streams at the bottom of this page! If you haven’t seen, for the entire month of November, we’ve been raising money for charity. We’re taking straight donations here for the University of Michigan Rogel Cancer Center , and we’re also holding an online auction to benefit the House of Providence. You can see the auction items here . But on Saturday — from 8 a.m. ET to midnight— we’re going all out. We’re trying to raise as much money for charity while also having a ton of fun talking Lions football with a bunch of special guests. As a reminder, here are the specific donation goals we’re hoping to hit this year: $5,000 — Activates PODcast host punishment by Lions (see below) MET! $10,000 — POD team runs a 5k MET! $15,000 — POD staff has to reveal high school photos $20,000 — JCPenney-style photoshoot, resulting in a POD calendar (available for $750 donation) $25,000 — POD team does public karaoke of Toto’s “Africa” $30,000 — Jeremy learns and records a TikTok dance $35,000 — Jeremy reveals a comedy sketch from his past $40,000 — Jeremy gets frosted tips, a la Skyler Gill-Howard $45,000 — Ryan reveals college poetry $50,000 — Erik watches a 15-minute Aaron Rodgers highlight reel with “I <3 Aaron” shirt $60,000 — Jeremy dresses up like Marilyn Monroe $75,000 — Jeremy will grow out his hair for an entire year And here’s a look at our current schedule of guests for Saturday. Please note that these guests are subject to change, and we’re still looking to add more! Plus, the Pride of Detroit staff will make appearances all day! 8 a.m. ET – Justin Rogers of Detroit Football Network 8:30 a.m. – Richard Silva of the Detroit News 9 a.m. – Kory Woods of MLive 9:30 a.m. – Brad Galli of The Brad Galli Show 10 a.m. – Ben Raven of MLive 10:30 a.m. – Colton Pouncy of The Athletic 11 a.m. – Nolan Bianchi of the Detroit News 1 p.m. – Dan Miller, voice of Detroit Lions radio 2 p.m. – Will Burchfield, writer for 97.1 The Ticket 3 p.m. – Ryan Walsh, Grand Rapids radio host 5:30 p.m. – Nick Baumgardner, The Athletic 7 p.m. – Dave Birkett of the Detroit Free Press 11 p.m. – Ben Solak of ESPN Here’s everything you need to know about the stream: When: Saturday, November 28, 2026 Time: 8 a.m. ET through midnight Where: YouTube page Twitch Channel Donation link here For more information on our charity drive, check out our full page on details here. item.title: Alabama Gets Unexpected Iron Bowl News as Auburn Makes Last-Minute Changes
item.description: Oct 24, 2026; Tuscaloosa, Alabama, USA; Alabama Crimson Tide head coach Kalen DeBoer looks on against the Texas A&M Aggies during the second half at Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Leong-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) TUSCALOOSA, Ala. — Alabama’s final regular-season game suddenly has another storyline, and the latest developments could affect Saturday night’s Iron Bowl. Auburn released an updated SEC availability report Friday night, revealing significant changes involving two of its most important players. One development provides the Tigers with a major boost ahead of their trip to Bryant-Denny Stadium. However, the other leaves Auburn without a key defensive contributor against the Crimson Tide. With Alabama’s College Football Playoff positioning at stake, both updates could become important Saturday. Auburn Receives Major Quarterback Update Auburn quarterback Byrum Brown was upgraded from questionable to probable on Friday’s SEC availability report. The designation represents an encouraging development after Brown appeared on the injury report earlier in the week. According to On3’s Pete Nakos, Brown is expected to start Saturday against Alabama. However, his availability will not be finalized until the SEC releases its final pregame report. Brown has been one of Auburn’s most productive offensive players this season. The senior has completed 65.6% of his passes for 2,035 yards, 15 touchdowns and eight interceptions. Additionally, he has rushed for 644 yards and nine touchdowns. His dual-threat ability provides Auburn with another dimension against Alabama’s defense. Another Auburn Star Receives Disappointing News While Brown’s status improved, linebacker De’Marcus Riddick received a less encouraging update. Riddick was downgraded from questionable to out Friday night. The Auburn defender has been dealing with an ankle injury that has prevented him from returning to action. His absence could become particularly important against Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell. Russell has demonstrated the ability to extend plays with his legs, forcing opposing defenses to account for his mobility. Without Riddick, Auburn will need other defenders to assume additional responsibilities. The Tigers will also be without linebacker Bryce Deas and cornerback Gavin Jenkins. Consequently, Auburn enters the rivalry with several important defensive absences. Alabama Also Faces Injury Concerns Alabama has dealt with its own injury challenges entering the Iron Bowl. Defensive backs Jireh Edwards and Nick Sherman also remain unavailable. Meanwhile, linebacker Caleb Woodson and defensive lineman Devan Thompkins were listed as probable. item.content:encoded: Oct 24, 2026; Tuscaloosa, Alabama, USA; Alabama Crimson Tide head coach Kalen DeBoer looks on against the Texas A&M Aggies during the second half at Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Leong-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) TUSCALOOSA, Ala. — Alabama’s final regular-season game suddenly has another storyline, and the latest developments could affect Saturday night’s Iron Bowl. Auburn released an updated SEC availability report Friday night, revealing significant changes involving two of its most important players. One development provides the Tigers with a major boost ahead of their trip to Bryant-Denny Stadium. However, the other leaves Auburn without a key defensive contributor against the Crimson Tide. With Alabama’s College Football Playoff positioning at stake, both updates could become important Saturday. Auburn Receives Major Quarterback Update Auburn quarterback Byrum Brown was upgraded from questionable to probable on Friday’s SEC availability report. The designation represents an encouraging development after Brown appeared on the injury report earlier in the week. According to On3’s Pete Nakos, Brown is expected to start Saturday against Alabama. However, his availability will not be finalized until the SEC releases its final pregame report. Brown has been one of Auburn’s most productive offensive players this season. The senior has completed 65.6% of his passes for 2,035 yards, 15 touchdowns and eight interceptions. Additionally, he has rushed for 644 yards and nine touchdowns. His dual-threat ability provides Auburn with another dimension against Alabama’s defense. Another Auburn Star Receives Disappointing News While Brown’s status improved, linebacker De’Marcus Riddick received a less encouraging update. Riddick was downgraded from questionable to out Friday night. The Auburn defender has been dealing with an ankle injury that has prevented him from returning to action. His absence could become particularly important against Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell. Russell has demonstrated the ability to extend plays with his legs, forcing opposing defenses to account for his mobility. Without Riddick, Auburn will need other defenders to assume additional responsibilities. The Tigers will also be without linebacker Bryce Deas and cornerback Gavin Jenkins. Consequently, Auburn enters the rivalry with several important defensive absences. Alabama Also Faces Injury Concerns Alabama has dealt with its own injury challenges entering the Iron Bowl. The Crimson Tide listed seven players as out on Friday’s SEC availability report. Those players include offensive lineman Casey Poe, linebacker Cayden Jones, defensive lineman Jeremiah Beaman and tight end Josh Ford. Defensive backs Jireh Edwards and Nick Sherman also remain unavailable. Meanwhile, linebacker Caleb Woodson and defensive lineman Devan Thompkins were listed as probable. However, Alabama received encouraging news concerning Russell. The Crimson Tide quarterback was not listed on the injury report after dealing with an ankle issue earlier this month. Coach Kalen DeBoer previously indicated that he expected Russell to participate fully during Iron Bowl preparations. Auburn’s Quarterback Situation Could Change the Matchup Brown’s expected availability gives Auburn a different offensive outlook than it would have with a backup quarterback. The senior has started all 11 games for the Tigers this season. However, he played just two snaps during Auburn’s 59-17 victory over Samford last weekend. Backup quarterback Tristan Ti’a handled most of the offensive responsibilities. Ti’a completed 17 of 18 passes for 341 yards and four touchdowns. Although that performance provided encouragement, facing Alabama represents a considerably more difficult challenge. Brown’s experience and rushing ability could prove especially valuable against the Crimson Tide. Alabama’s Playoff Position Remains on the Line Alabama enters Saturday with a 9-2 record and a No. 6 ranking in the College Football Playoff standings. The Crimson Tide’s hopes of reaching the SEC Championship Game ended Friday after Texas defeated Texas A&M. However, Alabama remains in contention for a national championship. A victory over Auburn would allow the Crimson Tide to finish the regular season with 10 wins. Meanwhile, a loss could complicate Alabama’s playoff positioning heading into conference championship weekend. Auburn enters the matchup at 7-4 and has won three consecutive games. The Tigers would welcome an opportunity to damage their biggest rival’s postseason aspirations. How to Watch Auburn vs. Alabama Detail Information Game Auburn at Alabama Date Saturday, Nov. 28, 2026 Kickoff 7:30 p.m. ET TV channel ABC Stadium Bryant-Denny Stadium Location Tuscaloosa, Alabama The SEC’s final availability report is expected no later than 90 minutes before kickoff. That update should provide additional clarity concerning players listed as probable. Iron Bowl Receives Another Unexpected Twist The Iron Bowl rarely needs additional storylines. However, Auburn’s latest personnel developments add another layer of intrigue before Saturday’s meeting. The Tigers appear increasingly likely to have their starting quarterback available. At the same time, they must prepare to face Alabama without several defensive contributors. For the Crimson Tide, the stakes remain substantial. Alabama can strengthen its playoff position with a victory, while Auburn has an opportunity to deliver one of rivalry weekend’s biggest upsets. And with the final injury report still to come, both programs have one more important update awaiting them before kickoff. item.title: GB v Spain schedule, order of play and how to watch Davis Cup semi-final
item.description: Great Britain face Spain for a place in their first Davis Cup final since 2015, with Arthur Fery needing to beat Carlos Alcaraz in the singles. Leon Smith’s side stunned Germany in the quarter-finals on Thursday after doubles pair Henry Patten and Neal Skupski clinched the decider . Great Britain have not been in the Davis Cup final since Andy Murray led the team to its first title of the Open era 11 years ago. Alcaraz sat out Spain’s quarter-final win over Austria as he nurses a hamstring injury after winning the ATP Finals last weekend. Spain are the favourites to win the Davis Cup with two top-10 singles players in their line-up, in Alcaraz and Rafael Jodar. Jodar got Spain off to a winning start, overcoming the British No 2 Cameron Norrie 6-2 7-5 in the opening rubber. The winner of the semi-final in Bologna will play hosts and defending champions Italy, after they overcame Czechia. Here’s everything you need to know How to watch Davis Cup The semi-final against Spain will be shown on the BBC Sport website and BBC iPlayer, with the tie starting at 11am BST (12pm local time). Order of play From 11am Singles 1: Rafael Jodar bt Cameron Norrie 6-2 7-5 Followed by Singles 2: Arthur Fery v Carlos Alcaraz (If required) Doubles: Patten/Skupski v Martinez/Granollers Preview: Fery backed to ‘take risks’ in ‘free hit’ Leon Smith has told Arthur Fery to have no regrets if he gets the chance to play Carlos Alcaraz in the Davis Cup semi-finals. Great Britain’s upset win over Germany in Bologna on Thursday set up a mouth-watering clash with Spain as Smith’s side bid to reach the final for the first time since claiming the title in 2015. Fery will be playing just his fourth match in the competition but is set to face the World No 1 and No 3 back-to-back after losing to Alexander Zverev on Thursday. Alcaraz sat out Spain’s quarter-final win over Austria having won the ATP Finals last weekend despite nursing knee and hamstring issues but it would be a surprise if he did not play singles – and potentially doubles – on Saturday. Spain captain David Ferrer was keeping his cards close to his chest, saying: “I will see on Saturday. I don’t know yet. But it could be possible.” Mixing in such circles is another indication of Fery’s meteoric rise this season, and he was clearly disappointed not to be able to threaten Zverev. Arthur Fery will take on Carlos Alcaraz in the Davis Cup semi-finals (Getty) Smith said: “I think it’s another chance for him to go out and see what it feels like, then figure out ways that he can actually hurt Carlos. “The more matches he gets at this level, which is still very, very new for him… I think embrace it, don’t be scared of it. “People hate hearing this ‘free hit’ thing. It kind of is. Just go out, express yourself. Don’t come off the court with any regrets. Try to play safe in any way? No. Go and play. Go and take some risks. Shot make. Enjoy it.” Fery has not taken a set off Zverev in three meetings but this will be his first chance

item.title: “I’m Just like Shaq Free-Throw Shooting-Wise” – Victor Wembanyama Humbly Admits to Struggling at the Line As Lakers Legend Catches Stray
item.description: Shaquille O'Neal, Victor Wembanyama © X/ @Lakers, @spurs San Antonio Spurs superstar Victor Wembanyama admitted he was struggling at the free-throw line and compared himself to Los Angeles Lakers legend Shaquille O’Neal. Wembanyama missed five of his eight attempts at the line in Friday’s 99-96 win over the Lakers, including a crucial one up-three with 57 seconds left. Stephon Castle saved Wembanyama by knocking down a 3 and giving the Spurs a six-point lead. Wembanyama missed another free throw up two with just over two seconds left, but made his final attempt that sealed the Spurs’ win. Dissecting his underwhelming display at the charity stripe, Wembanyama told Prime Video analysts he was like O’Neal at the free-throw line. “I gotta say, I’m just like Shaq free-throw shooting-wise right now,” he said. O’Neal was one of the worst free-throw shooters in the league, and teams often fouled him in the clutch because of it. O’Neal was often benched when opponents played the foul game while trailing in close games. The Lakers legend shot 52.7% from the free-throw line. Wembanyama is much better over his career. Entering Friday’s game, he was a career 81.3% free-throw shooter and 77.8% on the season. Although it’s a career-low mark, Wembanyama is still one of the better shooting bigs in the NBA from the free-throw line. Victor Wembanyama’s elite rebounding allows Spurs to complete comeback win over Lakers Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs trailed by 20 points in the first half. However, they crawled back in the second half, inspired by Wembanyama’s elite two-way display. After managing only eight points and five rebounds in the first half, Wembanyama bounced back with 17 points and 11 rebounds in the second. His rebounding was decisive in that stretch. The Lakers won the 50-50 battles in the first half, but once Wembanyama locked in, there wasn’t much Los Angeles could do to stop the reigning Defensive Player of the Year. Wembanyama finished with 25 points, 16 rebounds, four steals and two blocks, overcoming an inefficient shooting night with hustle and effort in other areas. Wembanyama may have also got the edge in the MVP race against rival Luka Doncic. While Doncic had the better scoring night with 31 points on 45.2% shooting, the loss, coupled with his decision-making in the momentum-swinging third quarter, could have tipped the scales. Wembanyama, on the other hand, played more efficiently, giving the Spurs a better chance to win. item.title: Detroit Lions’ playoff, NFC North odds still high despite loss to Bears
item.description: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 26: Penei Sewell #58 of the Detroit Lions gives a speech in the team huddle prior to an NFL football game against the Chicago Bears at Ford Field on November 26, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions’ loss to the Chicago Bears was deflating and disappointing. Not so much because it was a critical game for Detroit’s playoff odds, but because the Lions were in a prime position to win and take a stranglehold on the division. But as you’ll soon see, the Lions are still in a great position to accomplish everything in front of them. Let’s look at how their playoff, NFC North, and even Super Bowl odds have shifted after their Thanksgiving loss to the Bears. Postseason odds: NYT simulator: 78% (down 8%) RBSDM: 81% (down 4%) DVOA: 83.3% (down 6.3%) ESPN (FPI): 91.5% (down 5.5%) Even by the most pessimistic models, the Lions still have more than a 3-in-4 chance to make the postseason. Their loss to the Bears did not decrease their postseason odds by more than 10% across any of these four prediction models. ESPN still remains very high on the Lions, with a massive 91.5% chance to make the playoffs, but it seems like the more normal average is around 80-83%. NFC North title odds NYT simulator: 15% (down 14%) RBSDM: 20% (down 13%) DVOA: 19.3% (down 18%) ESPN (FPI): 30.6% (down 19.4%) Obviously, this loss had a bigger impact on Detroit’s chances to win the division, but the odds are not outstandingly long still. The Lions still have a 15-30% chance to win the NFC North, and that stands true because they still have three division games left. And while they’re all on the road, Detroit has proven they can go toe-to-toe with any of those teams. And the fact that Detroit has a 2-1 record in the division already gives them a nice leg up on the tiebreakers, as long as they continue to beat their divisional foes. NFC’s No. 1 seed NYT simulator: 4% (down 4%) RBSDM: 6% (down 6%) DVOA: 3.9% (down 6.3%) ESPN : 5% (down 6%) You can pretty much kiss the Lions’ odds for the No. 1 seed goodbye. Unless the San Francisco 49ers struggle down the stretch—and they do have tough games against the Seahawks, Giants, Rams, and Chiefs left—Detroit is not likely to finish any higher than the NFC’s No. 2 seed. Super Bowl appearance odds ESPN (FPI): 11.0% (down 1.9%) DVOA: 7.3% (down 3.1%) Surprisingly, the Lions’ Super Bowl odds have not been impacted too much. Perhaps their strong offensive performance against a decent Bears defense has fed the models’ optimism about Detroit being able to survive a shootout game. However, their defensive performance on Thursday looms large as well.
item.content:encoded: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 26: Penei Sewell #58 of the Detroit Lions gives a speech in the team huddle prior to an NFL football game against the Chicago Bears at Ford Field on November 26, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions’ loss to the Chicago Bears was deflating and disappointing. Not so much because it was a critical game for Detroit’s playoff odds, but because the Lions were in a prime position to win and take a stranglehold on the division. But as you’ll soon see, the Lions are still in a great position to accomplish everything in front of them. Let’s look at how their playoff, NFC North, and even Super Bowl odds have shifted after their Thanksgiving loss to the Bears. Postseason odds: NYT simulator: 78% (down 8%) RBSDM: 81% (down 4%) DVOA: 83.3% (down 6.3%) ESPN (FPI): 91.5% (down 5.5%) Even by the most pessimistic models, the Lions still have more than a 3-in-4 chance to make the postseason. Their loss to the Bears did not decrease their postseason odds by more than 10% across any of these four prediction models. ESPN still remains very high on the Lions, with a massive 91.5% chance to make the playoffs, but it seems like the more normal average is around 80-83%. NFC North title odds NYT simulator: 15% (down 14%) RBSDM: 20% (down 13%) DVOA: 19.3% (down 18%) ESPN (FPI): 30.6% (down 19.4%) Obviously, this loss had a bigger impact on Detroit’s chances to win the division, but the odds are not outstandingly long still. The Lions still have a 15-30% chance to win the NFC North, and that stands true because they still have three division games left. And while they’re all on the road, Detroit has proven they can go toe-to-toe with any of those teams. And the fact that Detroit has a 2-1 record in the division already gives them a nice leg up on the tiebreakers, as long as they continue to beat their divisional foes. NFC’s No. 1 seed NYT simulator: 4% (down 4%) RBSDM: 6% (down 6%) DVOA: 3.9% (down 6.3%) ESPN : 5% (down 6%) You can pretty much kiss the Lions’ odds for the No. 1 seed goodbye. Unless the San Francisco 49ers struggle down the stretch—and they do have tough games against the Seahawks, Giants, Rams, and Chiefs left—Detroit is not likely to finish any higher than the NFC’s No. 2 seed. Super Bowl appearance odds ESPN (FPI): 11.0% (down 1.9%) DVOA: 7.3% (down 3.1%) Surprisingly, the Lions’ Super Bowl odds have not been impacted too much. Perhaps their strong offensive performance against a decent Bears defense has fed the models’ optimism about Detroit being able to survive a shootout game. However, their defensive performance on Thursday looms large as well.

item.title: Red Sox Signing Brandon Lowe Would Hurt the Yankees Even More
item.description: Red Sox Signing Brandon Lowe Would Hurt the Yankees Even More originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Red Sox have spent this offseason trying to put themselves in a position to win the AL East, though so has every other team in the best division in baseball. Jazz Chisholm Jr. signing with the Blue Jays has only added to that. While the Yankees lost a good player and a rival in Toronto landed one, the Red Sox could be affected. Or, they could hurt the Yankees even more by signing Brandon Lowe. With Chisholm gone, the Yankees have a hole at second base, and Lowe seems like one option to fill it. Ultimately, this is the type of move that helps in more ways than one, as the Red Sox would improve their own lineup and take something away from their biggest rival. Lowe fits Boston's roster as a left-handed bat with big power who can play second base. Despite a somewhat crowded infield, the Red Sox’s offense is always looking for ways to improve. He has been an elite hitter when healthy, and any contending lineup could use more of that. While the Red Sox aren’t going to make a move just to impact the Yankees, it does raise questions about how much sense this would make. The only issue Boston might consider is that Lowe was also offered the qualifying offer, similar to Jake Bauers, who it already signed. Signing Lowe would cost the Red Sox more draft picks, though his 35-home-run production would make up for it. item.title: Aston Villa Starting XI vs Ipswich Town: Confirmed Team News and Predicted Lineup
item.description: Aston Villa Starting XI vs Ipswich Town: Confirmed Team News and Predicted Lineup Aston Villa Predicted XI vs Ipswich Town as Unai Emery Eyes Reset at Portman Road Aston Villa head to Portman Road needing a correction, not another excuse. The recent run has been poor, the attacking output has been worse, and Unai Emery has decisions to make before facing Gary O’Neil’s Ipswich Town. The numbers tell the story. Villa had 55 per cent possession in the 1-0 defeat at RAMS Park and still failed to create a chance worth talking about. That is the issue. Possession without purpose is dead weight. Emery’s side have drifted into that trap across a damaging sequence of results against Fulham, Barcelona, Manchester United, Sunderland and Galatasaray. Saturday is not about style points. It is about restoring some basic attacking function. Defensive changes look likely Zion Suzuki is expected to keep his place in goal. In front of him, Villa may go back to experience and familiarity. Matty Cash could return at right-back, while Pau Torres may also come back into the side. That would be rough on Tyrone Mings and Taylor Harwood-Bellis, particularly after they combined for 15 defensive actions in midweek. Still, selection is not a reward scheme. Emery needs balance, and Torres offers cleaner progression from the back. Victor Lindelof should keep his place, and Ian Maatsen may continue on the left despite a zero per cent cross accuracy in the last match. It is not ideal, but Villa’s problems have gone well beyond one full-back’s delivery. Boubacar Kamara remains the obvious holding midfielder. Four defensive actions and four duel wins against Galatasaray underlined his value. He does the ugly work and, right now, Villa need someone doing it. Midfield tweak could sharpen Aston Villa Photo IMAGO The obvious midfield call is Ross Barkley for Joao Gomes. Villa have lacked progressive passing into the front line, and that matters when chance creation has become such a glaring weakness. Gomes brings industry, but the game is asking for more incision. Barkley is the logical fix if Emery wants cleaner progression through central areas. It is a practical change, not a glamorous one, but Villa need practical solutions. Attack needs movement and clarity Further forward, Ibrahim Mbaye could replace Alysson on the left after another ineffective display. If the aim is to inject directness, that switch makes sense. He had little impact from the flank against Galatasaray, and the stat that stands out is brutal, he did not record a single touch in the opposition penalty area. Villa need better passing, quicker support around the striker and far more threat between the lines. If Emery gets that, they have enough to win. If not, the pressure only grows.

item.title: Ian Rapoport shares what he now knows about Brock Purdy’s ankle injury
item.description: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images Brock Purdy recently suffered an ankle sprain but the quarterback’s injury is not expected to be a major problem. Purdy has put himself in the NFL MVP conversation this season en route to the San Francisco 49ers going 9-1. He has a 71.0 completion rate and the joint-second-highest average yards per pass (9.0) in the NFL right now, which is only bettered by Lamar Jackson (10.0 in five games). The 49ers will have to make do without Purdy against the Seattle Seahawks this weekend but it doesn’t appear as though the QB will be sidelined for too long. Brock Purdy’s injury not considered ‘major’ Speaking on the NFL Network this week, Ian Rapoport commented on the 26-year-old’s injury and said that it is ‘not considered to be major’. He stated: “Brock Purdy has not yet practised for the San Francisco 49ers. He’s dealing with an ankle sprain. It’s not considered to be major, but if a starting quarterback doesn’t practise at all, you don’t think he has a chance to play.” WebMD have previously reported that Grade 1 ankle sprains take around 1-3 weeks to recover from. Grade 2 could take 4-6 weeks and a Grade 3 could rule an NFL player out for ‘several months’. However, based on Rapoport’s comments saying Purdy’s issue is not ‘major’, it looks as though his problem would be classified in the Grade 1 category. After this week’s game with the Seahawks, the 49ers are next in action on December 6 against the New York Giants. They will then play the Los Angeles Rams on December 13 before clashing with the Los Angeles Chargers on December 17. Purdy could miss all three of those games if his injury recovery time is on the higher end of a Grade 1 sprain, but there is also a chance he could be back in a week’s time to face the Giants. item.title: 'I am not prepared': Rohit Sharma reveals how he agreed to return as Mumbai Indians captain
item.description: NEW DELHI: Veteran batter Rohit Sharma is back in charge of Mumbai Indians after a three-year hiatus, but the five-time IPL-winning captain says his return was not driven by a desire to reclaim the leadership role. It was the feeling that the franchise needed direction after a difficult few seasons. Rohit was on Friday reinstated as Mumbai Indians captain ahead of the 2027 edition of the Indian Premier League. He will succeed Hardik Pandya, who has joined Punjab Kings in a trade involving pacer Arshdeep Singh. Rohit, who led Mumbai to five IPL titles, admitted that he was initially unsure about taking up the responsibility again. The decision came after discussions with the franchise management and some thought about the team's future. "My honest thought initially was, I am not prepared for this right now. I have to go back and think about it kyunki kaafi kuch ho chuka tha. Toh I don't know if I was in that frame of mind to do it or not," Rohit said in an interview. However, he eventually felt that the team needed someone to take it forward. "But then andar se feeling aisa aaya ki yaar I am not saying that this team needs me as a leader, but this team needs a direction right now. And whatever that direction is, if it is me, I am more than happy to drive this team forward," he added. 'That's not MI' Rohit's decision came against the backdrop of a disappointing run for Mumbai Indians. After winning the IPL in 2020, the franchise struggled to reproduce its earlier success. Mumbai finished fifth in 2021 and 10th in 2022 under Rohit. They reached Qualifier 2 in 2023 before the management decided to make a change in leadership, with Pandya replacing Rohit. The change did not bring the desired results either. Mumbai finished 10th in 2024, reached Qualifier 2 in 2025 and ended the 2026 season in ninth place. Rohit said the team's struggles had frustrated several players and made him reflect on how Mumbai could return to its old standards. "Look, I mean as soon as we finished the IPL, we had a very disappointing season and I was like not just me but many other players were quite frustrated with how we were playing," he said. "Main ghar gaya, I thought about it ki yaar it's not the team that used to be once upon a time. We need to get back to that. How can we do that? It happens to any team when you have seen such a high, there is bound to be a low." The 39-year-old was particularly concerned that Mumbai were not competing at the level expected of a franchise that had enjoyed so much success. "Disappointment qualification ka nahi hai. Disappointment tha ki hum theek se khel nahi rahe the. Jo responsibility the logon ke paas woh theek se ho nahi raha tha," he said. "Which again you know it's a very natural thing to happen. It was the feeling that the franchise needed direction after a difficult few seasons. Rohit was on Friday reinstated as Mumbai Indians captain ahead of the 2027 edition of the Indian Premier League. He will succeed Hardik Pandya, who has joined Punjab Kings in a trade involving pacer Arshdeep Singh. Rohit, who led Mumbai to five IPL titles, admitted that he was initially unsure about taking up the responsibility again. The decision came after discussions with the franchise management and some thought about the team's future. "My honest thought initially was, I am not prepared for this right now. I have to go back and think about it kyunki kaafi kuch ho chuka tha. Toh I don't know if I was in that frame of mind to do it or not," Rohit said in an interview. However, he eventually felt that the team needed someone to take it forward. "But then andar se feeling aisa aaya ki yaar I am not saying that this team needs me as a leader, but this team needs a direction right now. And whatever that direction is, if it is me, I am more than happy to drive this team forward," he added. 'That's not MI' Rohit's decision came against the backdrop of a disappointing run for Mumbai Indians. After winning the IPL in 2020, the franchise struggled to reproduce its earlier success. Mumbai finished fifth in 2021 and 10th in 2022 under Rohit. They reached Qualifier 2 in 2023 before the management decided to make a change in leadership, with Pandya replacing Rohit. The change did not bring the desired results either. Mumbai finished 10th in 2024, reached Qualifier 2 in 2025 and ended the 2026 season in ninth place. Rohit said the team's struggles had frustrated several players and made him reflect on how Mumbai could return to its old standards. "Look, I mean as soon as we finished the IPL, we had a very disappointing season and I was like not just me but many other players were quite frustrated with how we were playing," he said. "Main ghar gaya, I thought about it ki yaar it's not the team that used to be once upon a time. We need to get back to that. How can we do that? It happens to any team when you have seen such a high, there is bound to be a low." The 39-year-old was particularly concerned that Mumbai were not competing at the level expected of a franchise that had enjoyed so much success. "Disappointment qualification ka nahi hai. Disappointment tha ki hum theek se khel nahi rahe the. Jo responsibility the logon ke paas woh theek se ho nahi raha tha," he said. "Which again you know it's a very natural thing to happen. You know when you are losing, the momentum is not with you, the other teams are playing well, they are trying and capitalising more on you, putting pressure more on you and we were not responding to that pressure. And that includes everyone, not just one or two players. The entire MI was failing." A team he helped build Rohit said he discussed the situation with his wife before meeting Akash Ambani and other members of the management to explore ways of taking the team forward. "And then obviously I, Akash, Rank me up, we met, we discussed how to take this team forward, what can be done and all of that. A lot of ideas that came across," he said. The captaincy offer made him think about the responsibility he had carried for more than a decade and the connection he had built with the franchise. "But then itne saare cheezein sochne ke baad I realised ki yaar, you know, this is the team that you built. You know, for 10 years you captain this team. I mean I think it's time you try and accept that challenge again," Rohit said. He also pointed to Mumbai's three bottom-of-the-table finishes in the last five seasons as a reason why he felt he could not simply watch from the sidelines. "And to see that MI languishing at the bottom of the table for three seasons. One was during my tenure as well in 2022, then in 2024 and then 2026. That's not MI. That is not what MI is known for." Rohit, who became Mumbai captain in 2013, led the franchise to titles in 2013, 2015, 2017, 2019 and 2020. He was removed from the role after the 2023 season, when Pandya was brought in as captain. The right-hander, who began his IPL career with the erstwhile Deccan Chargers, has scored 7,329 runs in 281 matches, including two centuries and 49 half-centuries. He is the second-highest run-getter in the tournament behind Royal Challengers Bengaluru's Virat Kohli, who has 9,336 runs from 283 matches. Rohit is not promising an overnight turnaround, though. He acknowledged that leading an IPL side comes with its own challenges, particularly when players from different backgrounds have to come together as a unit. "So I am not going to sit here and say abhi main aa gaya hoon, sab change ho jayega. Ye it's obviously you know leading any team is never an easy job. It's the most tough thing and specially in IPL it's the toughest because there are so many different people who come and play for you," he said. He is, however, excited about the challenge of bringing Mumbai back to the level at which they were once known to compete. Rohit said in a statement issued by Mumbai Indians: "I am ready for the 20th season (of IPL), to the challenges ahead, and to giving our Paltan plenty of moments to celebrate. The focus will be on playing our brand of cricket, competing together and enjoying the game."

item.title: Cody Rhodes Teases Fresh Direction... (WWE News)
item.description: WWE.com Cody Rhodes has lifted the lid on his wish to front a 4-strong faction on WWE screens someday. The 'American Nightmare' talked about this dream on Stephanie McMahon's 'What's Your Story?' podcast , but he's unsure on the best way to pitch it. So, Cody has been feeding his thoughts into AI and seeing what apps have to say about it. He didn't reveal who ChatGPT thinks should be in his stable though, the big spoilsport. Seriously though, this is all food for thought, and it's rather interesting considering what Rhodes is doing at this year's Survivor Series: WarGames PLE . There, he's the captain/co-captain of 'Team USA' alongside CM Punk, Seth Rollins, LA Knight and Je'Von Evans. Would any of those men make it into Cody's group? It's possible. He's also spoken about working with Carmelo Hayes before, but it's unlikely Melo would be involved now he's part of The 946 over on Raw. To add to the intrigue, Rhodes told Stephanie that his faction has been "loosely pitched", but not by him. So, either a member of WWE's creative team has the same sort of idea, or Cody happened to mention his scheme to someone and they've decided to run with it. He's also wary of leaning on AI a little too much , because it's fairly easy to tell when somebody has ChatGPT (for example) script something out for them. The former WWE Champ wants any pitch to be backed by his voice, not AI. - Join WhatCulture Wrestling+ on YouTube for exclusive behind-the-scenes content, membership badges, emojis, and much, much more: https://www.youtube.com/@WhatCultureWrestling/join ! item.title: 'An embarrassing figure!' - Roberto Mancini takes aim at Serie A clubs as Italy crisis forces drastic youth gamble
item.description: FBL-EUR-NATIONS-ITA-FRA - AFP Roberto Mancini has blasted Serie A's "embarrassing" lack of domestic talent after being forced to call up inexperienced teenagers for Italy's Nations League campaign. With the national side missing out on the quarter-finals, the head coach admitted he must take bold risks to rebuild the squad. Mancini turns to youth in Nations League Mancini has revealed that a shortage of domestic players in Serie A left him little option but to hand international call-ups to youngsters with minimal top-flight experience. Speaking in an interview with Corriere dello Sport , the Italy coach addressed his recent squad selections. Ahead of this month's Nations League fixtures, Mancini drafted several teenagers into the national team camp, including youth players Riccardo Cassano and Simone Lontani. The move came during a mixed international window for Italy, who defeated France before a 4-1 loss to Belgium ended their hopes of reaching the quarter-finals. 'Embarrassing' Serie A numbers force change At the heart of Mancini's frustration is the shrinking pool of eligible players competing regularly in Italy's top division. With domestic representation dropping sharply, the coach believes he must look beyond established club regulars to keep the national side competitive. "I was forced to (call up young players), given that the proportion of Italian players in Serie A has fallen to 30%. It's an embarrassing figure," Mancini admitted. "I have no choice but to seek out young players with potential who are capable of developing." Club indifference and a 20-year problem Italy's current struggles come against a sobering recent backdrop. Despite being four-time world champions, the national side have failed to qualify for the last three World Cups. Against Belgium, Mancini showed his willingness to trust emerging talent by handing an international debut to 20-year-old striker Alphadjo Cisse, who has scored ten goals for AC Milan this season. Mancini insists the structural issue is nothing new and expects no favours from domestic teams. "I have to take risks by fielding them in important matches," he said. "The clubs have no interest in the national team, which has to find its own solutions. There's no point in complaining about the situation that has existed for at least 20 years, we simply have to scout for players and give them experience, even if it means risking a few defeats." A long-term gamble for Italy's future With their Nations League campaign over at the group stage, Italy now face a defining period of transition. The national team will continue scouting emerging prospects and fast-tracking them into senior international football. Although this approach carries the risk of short-term setbacks, Italy clearly hopes that this early experience will ultimately pay off on the biggest stage.
item.content:encoded: FBL-EUR-NATIONS-ITA-FRA - AFP Roberto Mancini has blasted Serie A's "embarrassing" lack of domestic talent after being forced to call up inexperienced teenagers for Italy's Nations League campaign. With the national side missing out on the quarter-finals, the head coach admitted he must take bold risks to rebuild the squad. Mancini turns to youth in Nations League Mancini has revealed that a shortage of domestic players in Serie A left him little option but to hand international call-ups to youngsters with minimal top-flight experience. Speaking in an interview with Corriere dello Sport , the Italy coach addressed his recent squad selections. Ahead of this month's Nations League fixtures, Mancini drafted several teenagers into the national team camp, including youth players Riccardo Cassano and Simone Lontani. The move came during a mixed international window for Italy, who defeated France before a 4-1 loss to Belgium ended their hopes of reaching the quarter-finals. 'Embarrassing' Serie A numbers force change At the heart of Mancini's frustration is the shrinking pool of eligible players competing regularly in Italy's top division. With domestic representation dropping sharply, the coach believes he must look beyond established club regulars to keep the national side competitive. "I was forced to (call up young players), given that the proportion of Italian players in Serie A has fallen to 30%. It's an embarrassing figure," Mancini admitted. "I have no choice but to seek out young players with potential who are capable of developing." Club indifference and a 20-year problem Italy's current struggles come against a sobering recent backdrop. Despite being four-time world champions, the national side have failed to qualify for the last three World Cups. Against Belgium, Mancini showed his willingness to trust emerging talent by handing an international debut to 20-year-old striker Alphadjo Cisse, who has scored ten goals for AC Milan this season. Mancini insists the structural issue is nothing new and expects no favours from domestic teams. "I have to take risks by fielding them in important matches," he said. "The clubs have no interest in the national team, which has to find its own solutions. There's no point in complaining about the situation that has existed for at least 20 years, we simply have to scout for players and give them experience, even if it means risking a few defeats." A long-term gamble for Italy's future With their Nations League campaign over at the group stage, Italy now face a defining period of transition. The national team will continue scouting emerging prospects and fast-tracking them into senior international football. Although this approach carries the risk of short-term setbacks, Italy clearly hopes that this early experience will ultimately pay off on the biggest stage.

item.title: Chad Johnson names the NFL team Aaron Rodgers could join immediately
item.description: Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images What happens next to Aaron Rodgers is the question on the lips of a lot of people around the NFL, following what has certainly been a dramatic week. The 42-year-old quarterback will have likely watched his former team, the Pittsburgh Steelers, comfortably beat the Denver Broncos on Friday. It was the first game that Mike McCarthy’s team has played since Rodgers was released. A lot of damage has now been done to Rodgers’ reputation, which was already far from flawless, with teams across the league left considering whether bringing in the opinionated free agent quarterback is actually worth the risk. Chad Johnson thinks Aaron Rodgers could join the Denver Broncos Although the reality is that a change at quarterback for the Broncos is unlikely, Nix’s performance on Friday in Pittsburgh was one worthy of being benched by Sean Payton for the remainder of the season. “So, do you think the Broncos are going to try and make a change at the QB spot?” Joe Johnson asked on Nightcap. Shannon Sharpe: “No. No, they’ve got Jared Stidham behind him. Absolutely not.” Chad Johnson: “Hey, you know, Aaron Rodgers is right there, though.” Sharpe: “That ain’t happening. Boy, you think he’ll pull that with Sean Payton?” Johnson: “Aaron Rodgers, hold on. Aaron Rodgers knows better than to play with Sean Payton. H***, I ain’t even played for Sean Payton, and I know not to play with Sean.” Benching Nix and bringing in Rodgers, and the media frenzy he would drag to Denver with him, would certainly be a statement by the Broncos. Friday was, however, a huge opportunity for the Broncos to open up a gap on the Kansas City Chiefs following their loss to the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving. The Broncos need a much higher level from their quarterback if they are going to make any waves in the postseason. Whether Rodgers would offer that is an entirely different question, with the veteran having a lot more than just football on his mind right now after his Steelers saga. item.title: ‘They took this public’: Aaron Rodgers fires back at Tom Brady after locker room remarks
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Aaron Rodgers has insisted that when his football career is over, he’ll go quietly into the background. However, after an ugly exit from the Pittsburgh Steelers, including a benching, a tell-all call on The Pat McAfee Show, and his subsequent release, Rodgers is making sure his voice is heard and that he has a say in the narrative. During Thursday’s call of the Dallas Cowboys-Philadelphia Eagles game, Fox analyst and seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady was critical of Aaron Rodgers calling into McAfee’s show to air out his grievances. “The sanctity of an NFL locker room is a very sacred place, and we shouldn’t ever lose track of that as players,” Brady said. “It’s a privilege to be in that locker room. You’re fighting with your teammates. You’re fighting with your coaches, you’re always acting as a team together and shouldn’t always be the place for, you know, private things to become public. That’s what I’ll say.” “The sanctity of an NFL locker room, it’s a very sacred place” Tom Brady takes issue with how Aaron Rodgers handled his Steelers benching on Wednesday https://t.co/gRRpgcKo41 — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 27, 2026 Rodgers’ former team hosted the Denver Broncos on Friday, and Rodgers made sure that he got the final word as far as “sanctity” goes. This time, Rodgers sent a text to Prime Video play-by-play man Al Michaels, who was on the call for Friday’s game. “Been the only story in town, of course, the Aaron Rodgers saga,” Michaels said during his broadcast of the Steelers’ 27-5 win over Denver. “Earlier today, I heard from Aaron, who said, he said, ‘A lot of talk about the sanctity of the locker room.’ “He said, ‘The code or sanctity exists to protect the integrity of the locker room, not to provide immunity from accountability for its leadership.’ He then also said, ‘They took this public. Never heard from the head coach. Then they leak at 11 p.m. They also barred me from the facility. That’s why I went to McAfee.” For his part, even as Rodgers does his best to control the narrative, Michaels feels that the quarterback’s legacy has taken a hit. If this is truly it for Rodgers, it was an ugly end to what was an extraordinary career. The post ‘They took this public’: Aaron Rodgers fires back at Tom Brady after locker room remarks appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: Matt Coronato’s Return to New York Brings Back Memories of a Rare Feat in Flames History
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Matt Coronato scored his seventh goal of the season Friday against the New Jersey Devils, giving the Calgary Flames forward goals in back-to-back games heading into Saturday’s matchup against the New York Rangers. The Long Island native has a little more reason to look forward to playing at Madison Square Garden than most of his teammates, though. The last time Coronato made his way through all three NHL arenas in the New York area on the same road trip, he accomplished something only Jarome Iginla had done in Flames history. Coronato joined Iginla in the Flames’ record books The Flames were fighting for a playoff spot in March 2025 when they visited the Rangers, Devils and New York Islanders in a span of five days. Coronato entered the trip with 16 goals on the season and left with 20, helping the Flames collect all six available points. As FlamesNation’s Ryan Pike pointed out at the time , Coronato became just the second player in franchise history to score in all three New York-area arenas on the same road trip. Iginla was the first to do it in December 1999. Part of what makes the feat so rare is that Calgary had only played all three teams on the same road trip seven times since the Devils relocated to New Jersey in 1982. Coronato scored the game-winning goal on the power play against the Rangers on March 18, beating Igor Shesterkin from the slot. Two nights later, an attempted pass to Nazem Kadri deflected off Dawson Mercer’s stick and beat former Flames goaltender Jacob Markstrom. Coronato saved his best performance for the team he grew up cheering for, scoring twice against the Islanders on March 22. He opened the scoring just 36 seconds into the game before scoring his 20th goal of the season in the second period. The four goals accounted for 20% of Coronato’s production through that point in the season, and he did it in his first NHL appearances in all three buildings. While reaching the 20-goal mark for the first time in his career would’ve been special regardless of where it happened, doing it against his childhood team with family in the area made for a pretty memorable week. Coronato is finding his scoring touch again Coronato’s goal against New Jersey on Friday came after some good work below the goal line by Morgan Frost and Aydar Suniev, the latter of whom was one of two players Calgary received in the Tyler Toffoli trade . Coronato found some open ice in the slot and beat Jake Allen to tie the game at 2-2. The Flames forward is up to seven goals and 12 assists through Calgary’s first 27 games of the season. He’s been more productive as a playmaker than a goal scorer to this point, but Calgary invested $45.5 million in Coronato over seven years in large part because of his ability to put the puck in the net. Getting him going as a goal scorer would be a big help for a team that’s still trying to figure out where most of its offense will come from in the coming years. The schedule won’t give Corona

item.title: Greg Sankey Faces New Legal Trouble as LSU Dispute Takes Unexpected Turn
item.description: SEC commissioner Greg Sankey talks during a press conference before a celebration for OU joining the Southeastern Conference in Norman, Okla., Monday, July 1, 2024. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) BATON ROUGE, La. — SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey is facing another serious development in his escalating dispute with LSU. However, this time, the controversy extends beyond his role as the conference’s commissioner. A newly amended lawsuit has placed Sankey himself at the center of a legal fight involving an LSU basketball player, with allegations that could carry personal financial consequences. The development comes just days before SEC university presidents and chancellors are scheduled to consider LSU’s future in the conference. Greg Sankey Personally Named in Amended Lawsuit Former LSU basketball player RJ Luis Jr. filed an amended lawsuit Wednesday, Nov. 25, naming Sankey as a defendant in both his official and personal capacities. According to reporting from Reuters and ESPN, Luis is seeking unspecified financial damages related to the SEC’s handling of his eligibility dispute. The filing also requests a jury trial. Luis’ attorneys allege that Sankey and the conference deliberately interfered with his opportunity to compete for LSU. They further contend that the commissioner acted with malice toward their client. Those claims remain allegations and have not been established in court. Nevertheless, the decision to name Sankey personally represents a significant escalation in the dispute. Lawsuit Alleges SEC Commissioner Threatened LSU The controversy centers on LSU’s decision to allow Luis to play basketball despite the SEC’s objections to his eligibility. Luis previously signed professional basketball contracts after his time at St. John’s. The SEC maintains eligibility standards restricting participation by athletes with certain professional experience. However, Luis obtained a Louisiana court injunction protecting his ability to compete without conference penalties. He subsequently made his LSU debut against Louisiana-Monroe on Nov. 18. Luis recorded 11 points and nine rebounds in 15 minutes. According to the amended lawsuit, Sankey communicated to LSU President Wade Rousse that the university could lose its SEC membership if Luis appeared in another game. The alleged communication occurred Nov. 19, one day after Luis’ debut. Rousse subsequently instructed LSU basketball coach Will Wade not to play Luis again. Luis’ attorneys argue that the conference’s actions effectively prevented their client from continuing his college basketball career. Luis is seeking compensation related to lost name, image and likeness opportunities, potential future earnings and damage to his professional prospects. item.content:encoded: SEC commissioner Greg Sankey talks during a press conference before a celebration for OU joining the Southeastern Conference in Norman, Okla., Monday, July 1, 2024. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) BATON ROUGE, La. — SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey is facing another serious development in his escalating dispute with LSU. However, this time, the controversy extends beyond his role as the conference’s commissioner. A newly amended lawsuit has placed Sankey himself at the center of a legal fight involving an LSU basketball player, with allegations that could carry personal financial consequences. The development comes just days before SEC university presidents and chancellors are scheduled to consider LSU’s future in the conference. Greg Sankey Personally Named in Amended Lawsuit Former LSU basketball player RJ Luis Jr. filed an amended lawsuit Wednesday, Nov. 25, naming Sankey as a defendant in both his official and personal capacities. According to reporting from Reuters and ESPN, Luis is seeking unspecified financial damages related to the SEC’s handling of his eligibility dispute. The filing also requests a jury trial. Luis’ attorneys allege that Sankey and the conference deliberately interfered with his opportunity to compete for LSU. They further contend that the commissioner acted with malice toward their client. Those claims remain allegations and have not been established in court. Nevertheless, the decision to name Sankey personally represents a significant escalation in the dispute. Lawsuit Alleges SEC Commissioner Threatened LSU The controversy centers on LSU’s decision to allow Luis to play basketball despite the SEC’s objections to his eligibility. Luis previously signed professional basketball contracts after his time at St. John’s. The SEC maintains eligibility standards restricting participation by athletes with certain professional experience. However, Luis obtained a Louisiana court injunction protecting his ability to compete without conference penalties. He subsequently made his LSU debut against Louisiana-Monroe on Nov. 18. Luis recorded 11 points and nine rebounds in 15 minutes. According to the amended lawsuit, Sankey communicated to LSU President Wade Rousse that the university could lose its SEC membership if Luis appeared in another game. The alleged communication occurred Nov. 19, one day after Luis’ debut. Rousse subsequently instructed LSU basketball coach Will Wade not to play Luis again. Luis’ attorneys argue that the conference’s actions effectively prevented their client from continuing his college basketball career. LSU Player Seeks Financial Damages The amended filing outlines several categories of alleged financial and personal harm. Luis is seeking compensation related to lost name, image and likeness opportunities, potential future earnings and damage to his professional prospects. His attorneys also cite alleged emotional distress and reputational harm. Additionally, the lawsuit seeks legal expenses and potentially enhanced damages under Louisiana law. However, the filing does not specify a total dollar amount. The court has not determined whether Sankey or the SEC is liable for any of the alleged damages. SEC Faces Questions About Different Treatment of LSU The lawsuit also raises questions about how the conference has handled similar eligibility disputes involving other schools. Luis’ attorneys allege that athletes at 14 of the SEC’s 16 member institutions have competed under court orders this season. They further claim that eight SEC schools have rostered men’s basketball players whose eligibility was protected by court rulings. According to the filing, those institutions have not faced comparable threats concerning their conference membership. The allegations form part of Luis’ argument that LSU and its player received unequal treatment. However, the claims have not been resolved by the court. The SEC has defended its authority to establish and enforce eligibility standards agreed upon by member institutions. December 3 Meeting Could Bring Another Major Development The legal dispute comes as the SEC prepares for a meeting that could have enormous implications for LSU. Conference presidents and chancellors are scheduled to meet Thursday, Dec. 3, to consider terminating the university’s membership. LSU has been an SEC member since the conference’s founding in 1932. Removing the Tigers would represent an extraordinary development for one of college athletics’ most prominent conferences. However, no expulsion decision has been made. The matter would require a vote by conference leadership, rather than a unilateral decision by Sankey. Meanwhile, separate legal proceedings involving LSU and the SEC remain unresolved. A federal judge denied the conference’s request for emergency relief Wednesday, but the ruling does not prevent the Dec. 3 meeting from proceeding. Another Legal Fight Awaits Sankey and the SEC The amended lawsuit adds a personal dimension to a controversy that has already attracted national attention. What began as a disagreement over athlete eligibility now involves potential financial damages, competing court proceedings and questions about LSU’s conference membership. For Sankey, the latest filing means he must address allegations directed at his own conduct, not merely decisions attributed to the SEC. For LSU, the situation remains equally consequential. The Tigers face uncertainty about their conference future while the legal dispute continues. And with a critical meeting approaching, neither side has reached a resolution. The next chapter could have implications extending far beyond one basketball player or one university. Check out Week 13 College Football scores here: View our latest SEC Country articles here:

item.title: Atletico Madrid fix €35-40 million pricetag on Lookman
item.description: Atletico Madrid fix €35-40 million pricetag on Lookman Ademola Lookman could leave Atlético Madrid in January, with the club ready to evaluate offers. According to Fichajes.net , the Madrid club is seeking a fee between €35 and €40 million. Roma remains interested: Gasperini considers him the ideal addition, and the player wouldn’t mind working with the Grugliasco-based coach again. It remains to be seen whether Roma can meet Atlético’s demands.

item.title: Nations Championship finals weekend results, fixtures and hemisphere shield score
item.description: The inaugural Nations Championship has reached its climax with the finals weekend seeing six top-class international rugby matches across an action-packed three days at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham , with either South Africa or France set to be crowned the first-ever winner on Sunday evening The new competition has pitted the Six Nations sides against the four Rugby Championship competitors, plus Japan and Fiji, across six matches split evenly across the July and November Test windows, with all 12 teams having had their seedings for this finals weekend determined by those results. The Springboks topped the southern hemisphere table, while France did likewise in the northern hemisphere standings, meaning those two heavyweights will clash for the title at 4.40pm GMT on Sunday – in a rematch of their incredible battle in Paris, narrowly won by Les Bleus , earlier this month – with the victors lifting the Nations Championship trophy. Before that, there will be five other matches across three days with each country facing their equivalent finisher from the group stage – including tantalising match-ups such as England against the All Blacks and Scotland v Argentina . Meanwhile the two hemispheres will also battle for the Hemisphere Shield in a ‘Ryder Cup-style’ points system across the weekend. Here’s everything you need to know about finals weekend: Finals weekend results and fixtures - Allianz Stadium, Twickenham FRIDAY 27 NOVEMBER 6th vs 6th: Italy 23-21 Fiji 3rd vs 3rd: Ireland 38-14 Australia SATURDAY 28 NOVEMBER 5th vs 5th (1.10pm): Wales vs Japan 2nd vs 2nd (4.40pm): England vs New Zealand SUNDAY 29 NOVEMBER 4th vs 4th (1.10pm): Scotland vs Argentina 1st vs 1st – Nations Championship final (4.40pm): France vs South Africa What is the Hemisphere Shield? In addition to the Nations Championship itself, the Hemisphere Shield is also on offer as the northern hemisphere and southern hemisphere go head to head across the weekend. A ‘Ryder Cup-style’ points system will decide its fate with each victory in the matches featuring the second- to sixth-place finishers worth one point and victory in the Nations Championship final itself worth two points – meaning seven points are on offer and the first hemisphere to rack up four points will claim the Hemisphere Shield. In the event of a draw in the 6th vs 6th, 5th vs 5th, 4th vs 4th, 3rd vs 3rd or 2nd vs 2nd matches, the game will go to 10 minutes of golden point extra time (with the first team to score being declared the winners) and if neither side scores, each team will receive half a point towards the Hemisphere Shield. The final cannot end in a draw, so if the scores are still level after golden point extra time, then a place-kicking contest will occur to decide the champion. Hemisphere Shield latest score (first to four points wins) Northern Hemisphere 2-0 Southern Hemisphere How can I watch it? Viewers in the United Kingdom will be able to watch every game on ITV after the free-to-air broadcaster struck

The final cannot end in a draw, so if the scores are still level after golden point extra time, then a place-kicking contest will occur to decide the champion. Hemisphere Shield latest score (first to four points wins) Northern Hemisphere 2-0 Southern Hemisphere How can I watch it? Viewers in the United Kingdom will be able to watch every game on ITV after the free-to-air broadcaster struck a deal to show the competition. What is the Nations Championship? Announced during the 2023 Rugby World Cup, the new competition will be held every other year and replaces the traditional summer tours and Autumn Nations Series. It is designed to add context to the international calendar, with Fiji and Japan invited to join the Six Nations and Rugby Championship sides to form a top 12. Promotion and relegation is planned for the future with the second-tier Nations Cup, though will not take place in 2026. item.title: Rotherham defender Douglas joins Barrow on loan
item.description: Hamish Douglas has joined Barrow on a short-term loan [Getty Images] Barrow have signed Rotherham United defender Hamish Douglas on a short-term loan. The 21-year-old Millers academy product made 10 league appearances for Rotherham in League One last season and has featured three times in their current League Two campaign. Douglas has also gained experience out on loan with Warrington Town and Gainsborough Trinity. The versatile defender joins Barrow and has been registered in time to feature against Woking on Saturday.
