item.title: Alabama Faces Nightmare Iron Bowl Scenario That Could Change Its Entire Season
item.description: Nov 14, 2026; Nashville, Tennessee, USA; Alabama Crimson Tide head coach Kalen DeBoer stands and looks down field during a time out against the Vanderbilt Commodores during the second half at FirstBank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) TUSCALOOSA, Ala. — Alabama enters Saturday’s Iron Bowl with one championship opportunity already gone. However, Auburn has an opportunity to deliver an even more painful blow to the Crimson Tide. The annual rivalry returns to Bryant-Denny Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 28, with Alabama attempting to protect its College Football Playoff position. Meanwhile, Auburn has an opportunity to turn an otherwise disappointing season into an unforgettable one. And the Tigers could accomplish that by ruining their biggest rival’s postseason outlook. Alabama Already Received Bad News Before Iron Bowl Alabama entered rivalry weekend with an opportunity to reach the SEC Championship Game. However, the Crimson Tide needed help from other conference opponents. Texas’ victory over Texas A&M on Friday eliminated Alabama from the conference championship race. The Longhorns will face Georgia in Atlanta on Dec. 5. Consequently, Alabama must now pursue a national championship without another opportunity to improve its résumé in the SEC title game. That makes Saturday’s rivalry matchup especially important. A victory would allow Alabama to finish the regular season at 10-2. However, a loss would leave the Crimson Tide at 9-3 and introduce another layer of uncertainty into the playoff selection process. Auburn Could Deliver Alabama’s Worst-Case Scenario Auburn enters Saturday’s game at 7-4 following three consecutive victories. The Tigers most recently defeated Samford 59-17, producing one of their strongest offensive performances of the season. However, Saturday presents a considerably more difficult challenge. Alabama has won three consecutive games, outscoring those opponents by a combined 99-19. The Crimson Tide also enters the weekend ranked among the nation’s top College Football Playoff contenders. Nevertheless, the Iron Bowl has repeatedly demonstrated that records and expectations do not always determine the outcome. An Auburn victory would represent a major upset. More importantly, it would hand Alabama a third loss just before the playoff selection committee begins making its final decisions. Could Alabama Miss the College Football Playoff? Alabama currently holds a strong position in the playoff race. However, a third defeat could create significant uncertainty surrounding its postseason destination. The selection committee considers factors including overall record, strength of schedule, head-to-head results and performance against common opponents. Consequently, Alabama’s final ranking would depend partly on results elsewhere. A loss to Auburn would not automatically eliminate the Crimson Tide. However, it could place Alabama in a much more vulnerable position

Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) TUSCALOOSA, Ala. — Alabama enters Saturday’s Iron Bowl with one championship opportunity already gone. However, Auburn has an opportunity to deliver an even more painful blow to the Crimson Tide. The annual rivalry returns to Bryant-Denny Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 28, with Alabama attempting to protect its College Football Playoff position. Meanwhile, Auburn has an opportunity to turn an otherwise disappointing season into an unforgettable one. And the Tigers could accomplish that by ruining their biggest rival’s postseason outlook. Alabama Already Received Bad News Before Iron Bowl Alabama entered rivalry weekend with an opportunity to reach the SEC Championship Game. However, the Crimson Tide needed help from other conference opponents. Texas’ victory over Texas A&M on Friday eliminated Alabama from the conference championship race. The Longhorns will face Georgia in Atlanta on Dec. 5. Consequently, Alabama must now pursue a national championship without another opportunity to improve its résumé in the SEC title game. That makes Saturday’s rivalry matchup especially important. A victory would allow Alabama to finish the regular season at 10-2. However, a loss would leave the Crimson Tide at 9-3 and introduce another layer of uncertainty into the playoff selection process. Auburn Could Deliver Alabama’s Worst-Case Scenario Auburn enters Saturday’s game at 7-4 following three consecutive victories. The Tigers most recently defeated Samford 59-17, producing one of their strongest offensive performances of the season. However, Saturday presents a considerably more difficult challenge. Alabama has won three consecutive games, outscoring those opponents by a combined 99-19. The Crimson Tide also enters the weekend ranked among the nation’s top College Football Playoff contenders. Nevertheless, the Iron Bowl has repeatedly demonstrated that records and expectations do not always determine the outcome. An Auburn victory would represent a major upset. More importantly, it would hand Alabama a third loss just before the playoff selection committee begins making its final decisions. Could Alabama Miss the College Football Playoff? Alabama currently holds a strong position in the playoff race. However, a third defeat could create significant uncertainty surrounding its postseason destination. The selection committee considers factors including overall record, strength of schedule, head-to-head results and performance against common opponents. Consequently, Alabama’s final ranking would depend partly on results elsewhere. A loss to Auburn would not automatically eliminate the Crimson Tide. However, it could place Alabama in a much more vulnerable position entering conference championship weekend. Several other nationally ranked teams are also competing for limited playoff spots. Additionally, conference championship results could reshape the final bracket. Alabama would prefer to avoid relying on those outcomes. Auburn Has Nothing to Lose in Tuscaloosa The Tigers enter the Iron Bowl without an opportunity to compete for the SEC Championship. However, Auburn has already secured bowl eligibility. That gives the program an opportunity to approach Saturday’s rivalry with a different kind of motivation. The Tigers can improve their postseason destination while potentially damaging Alabama’s national championship ambitions. For Auburn fans, that combination would make a victory particularly satisfying. Auburn has struggled to match Alabama’s consistency in recent seasons. However, a road victory over the Crimson Tide would provide a significant statement heading into the offseason. Iron Bowl History Offers Alabama a Warning The Iron Bowl has produced some of college football’s most memorable upsets and dramatic finishes. In 2013, Auburn defeated Alabama on Chris Davis’ famous missed-field-goal return, ending the Crimson Tide’s undefeated season. Six years later, Auburn defeated Alabama 48-45 in another rivalry classic. Those games demonstrated how quickly the stakes can change when the programs meet. Saturday’s matchup offers another opportunity for an unexpected result. Alabama enters as the favorite, but Auburn has the chance to alter its rival’s postseason outlook. item.title: Celtics' Neemias Queta Could Force Difficult Mitchell Robinson Decision
item.description: Celtics' Neemias Queta Could Force Difficult Mitchell Robinson Decision originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Celtics decided to make a move that seemed to be one of the more impressive of the offseason when they signed Mitchell Robinson, the former Knicks NBA champion. To say that Robinson's time in Boston has gone as planned would be wrong, as he's been very below average, to say the least. The Celtics, however, are very fortunate that some other players have stepped up in his struggles, including Neemias Queta. Queta, who hasn't always been a player who the Celtics can count on, has been with Boston since 2023-2024. Before the 2025-26 season, he had started in only six games in his entire career. Last year he started in 75, and this year he started in 12 of the 17 he's played. Queta is playing better than ever, putting up career highs in multiple statistics, including 10.4 points per game. But it also raises the question of what the Celtics could do with Robinson. If there is any possibility of moving on from Robinson, somebody like Queta playing at this level definitely helps. If the Celtics hadn't gotten this type of production out of the big man, they would find themselves in one of the more difficult positions in the NBA because of it. Instead, the Celtics now have a player they can trade in a couple of weeks and should still get a somewhat decent package. Robinson likely isn't going to return multiple draft picks or anything of that sort, but he shouldn't have to be salary dumped. More Celtics news Celtics NBA Cup Clinching Scenarios Joe Mazzulla's New Starting Lineup Flashes Exciting Potential Tatum's Clutch Time Stats Rank Among NBA's Best

item.title: Ben Roethlisberger gives his verdict on Mason Rudolph’s first start after Aaron Rodgers release
item.description: Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers responded to Aaron Rodgers in emphatic fashion. After a week in which Aaron Rodgers was benched, publicly flamed head coach Mike McCarthy, and was subsequently released by the team, the Steelers sent a message to the four-time MVP that they are just fine without him. They beat the Denver Broncos 27-5 with backup Mason Rudolph at quarterback, an immensely impressive display against a team that made the AFC Championship game last season. Steelers’ legendary quarterback Ben Roethlisberger shared his honest thoughts on the game afterward, including his verdict on Rudolph’s performance in his first start without Rodgers on the team. Ben Roethlisberger’s honest verdict on Mason Rudolph’s performance against the Broncos Roethlisberger won two Super Bowls as the Steelers’ quarterback, so who better to assess Rudolph’s performance? On his podcast, Footbahlin, he said he was impressed by the 31-year-old’s showing. Roethlisberger said, “I will give a lot of kudos and credit to Mason Rudolph. He got thrown into a crazy situation: hey, you are now the starter, we are going to bench a gold jacket Hall of Fame guy, and you are now taking his job.” “We talked about it all the time on the show, the best backups in the world—guys that I played with, like Rob Gronkowski, Byron [Leftwich], Charlie Batch, Joshua Dobbs, Duck [Hodges], and Jones. “They were always ready to go. You prepare yourself to play, but also prepare the team and the other quarterback to get ready to go. They literally, in as coach Tom [Tomlin] would say, the 11th hour, said, ‘Hey, here you go.’ “Going into this game against a Denver football team that was 8-2, at the top of the AFC, a really good football team. DK [Metcalf] is probably the biggest fan right now of Aaron [Rodgers] because they took all the pressure off of him. “Mason Rudolph stepped up tonight. Was he great? No, but he did not have to be great. He had to do what was effective enough that we got the win.” Rudolph was solid in his game against the Broncos, completing nine of his 15 pass attempts, throwing for 142 yards, throwing a touchdown, and no interceptions. It was all he needed to deliver, with an elite defense holding the Broncos to no touchdowns and scoring two of their own. If the Steelers’ defense performs to that level from here on out, all they need is clean football from Rudolph. item.title: Ole Miss hits Mississippi State with a familiar Egg Bowl celebration seven years later
item.description: The peeing-dog celebration made another Egg Bowl appearance Friday in Oxford, Mississippi, late in the Ole Miss Rebels’ 41-17 win over the Mississippi State Bulldogs. The latest version came from a Rebels defensive tackle, who lifted his right leg after Ole Miss scored to go up 40-17 with 1:57 left. The extra point that followed closed the scoring. Will Echoles, the tackle, was borrowing a move with two very different endings in this rivalry. In 2017, receiver DK Metcalf mimicked a dog after a touchdown against Mississippi State and drew a penalty in a game Ole Miss won 31-28. In 2019, Elijah Moore did it after a 2-yard touchdown catch with four seconds left that pulled the Rebels within 21-20. Ole Miss hits a pee celebration in the Egg Bowl against Mississippi State. (via ABC) https://t.co/hxRx2MNexH — On3 (@On3) November 27, 2026 Jan 8, 2026; Glendale, AZ, USA; Mississippi Rebels defensive tackle Will Echoles (52) against the Miami Hurricanes during the 2026 Fiesta Bowl and semifinal game of the College Football Playoff at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Moore’s celebration drew a 15-yard unsportsmanlike conduct penalty that pushed the tying extra point back to 35 yards. Luke Logan missed it wide right, Mississippi State won 21-20, and Moore issued an apology the next day. “I apologize to my teammates, coaches and Rebel Nation for my actions at the end of the game. It was an emotional moment, and I deeply regret it. It does not represent who I am or who we are as a team, and I will grow stronger from this mistake,” Moore said in a statement. Coach Matt Luke and athletic director Keith Carter followed with a joint statement calling the celebration “disappointing and unacceptable.” Ole Miss has now won four straight Egg Bowls Echoles struck the pose after Ole Miss had turned a 10-6 halftime deficit into a rout, outscoring the Bulldogs 35-7 after the break. The Rebels led only 20-17 entering the fourth quarter, then scored the final 21 points, with Joshua Dye’s 1-yard run setting up the celebration. Fluff Bothwell ran for 129 yards on 18 carries for Mississippi State, and his 16-yard touchdown run in the second quarter gave the Bulldogs their first lead in an SEC game since Week 4 against the Missouri Tigers. Trinidad Chambliss completed 23 of 36 passes for 237 yards and two touchdowns and ran for another score. The win was the Rebels’ fourth in a row in the series and their sixth in the last seven meetings. The loss left Mississippi State at 5-7 for a second straight season and kept coach Jeff Lebby winless against Ole Miss in three tries. Pete Golding’s Rebels finished the regular season 8-4 and are waiting on their bowl assignment. Moore’s flag came with four seconds left in a one-point game. Echoles picked a 23-point lead and under two minutes to play, about as safe a moment as the Egg Bowl offers for that particular pose. item.title: Ilia Malinin fights for NHK Trophy title, extends Grand Prix figure skating win streak
item.description: Ilia Malinin followed his record short program by fighting through a strong free skate to win NHK Trophy, his ninth consecutive Grand Prix figure skating title dating to 2023. Malinin, the three-time world champion, doubled his planned quadruple flip to open his free skate to music from the animated series Blue Eye Samurai. He landed four quads later in his program, two of them a quarter under-rotated. It was still plenty enough as Malinin totaled 305.31 points and won by 34.82 over Frenchman Kevin Aymoz in Tokyo. "It felt like a battle out there, and I think it kind of represented the character that I play in this song," Malinin told the crowd. "I was not feeling the best today, but I tried my hardest to push through the whole program." FIGURE SKATING: Full Results | Broadcast Schedule Malinin beat his score from Saatva Skate America (284.31) and became the first man to break 300 points this Grand Prix season, which is now six events deep. Only the Grand Prix Final two weeks from now in China remains, which Malinin won the last three years. The Final takes the top six skaters per discipline over the six regular season events. It's the second-most prestigious annual competition after March's World Championships and the most exclusive. Earlier Saturday, Americans went one-two in ice dance with world bronze medalists Emilea Zingas and Vadym Kolesnik and Christina Carreira and Anthony Ponomarenko. Zingas and Kolesnik won with 203.29 points, the world's third-best total score over six Grand Prix regular season events. Only Olympic gold medalists Laurence Fournier Beaudry and Guillaume Cizeron of France's two scores this season have been higher. Zingas and Kolesnik and Fournier Beaudry and Cizeron will go head-to-head for the first time this season at the Grand Prix Final. Carreira and Ponomarenko, who were second or third at the last four U.S. Championships, finished second and third at their two Grand Prix starts this season to qualify for the Final for the first time in the sixth and last spot. Shin Ji-A of South Korea overtook Mone Chiba to win the women's NHK title and deny Japan a sweep of the six Grand Prix regular season women's titles. Shin, 18, made her first senior Grand Prix podium in her second season on the circuit. She's the first South Korean skater to win a Grand Prix since Kim Ye-Lim in 2022. But Shin did not qualify for the Final as her other Grand Prix result this fall — sixth at Skate Canada — wasn't strong enough. Chiba, who won Cup of China, fell on a downgraded triple loop in her NHK free skate, but still qualified for the Final in the third spot behind countrywomen Ami Nakai and Mao Shimada. They'll be joined at the Final by Alexandra Ignatova from Russia, Niina Petrokina from Estonia and Anastasiia Gubanova from Georgia. American Isabeau Levito is the first alternate. World champions Minerva Hase and Nikita Volodin won the pairs' event, just as they did at Skate America, to qualify for the Final. Ilia Malinin starts next figu

item.title: Urban Meyer gives common sense recommendation to USC’s Lincoln Riley ahead of UCLA game
item.description: The USC Trojans close the regular season Saturday against the UCLA Bruins with an 8-3 record, and losses to the Oregon Ducks, Wisconsin Badgers and Indiana Hoosiers have kept Lincoln Riley’s fifth season in Los Angeles under steady scrutiny. Urban Meyer, the former Ohio State coach who now works as a Fox Sports analyst, laid out what he would do about Riley on this week’s episode of The Triple Option, the podcast he hosts with Rob Stone and Mark Ingram II. Jan 20, 2025; Atlanta, GA, USA; Urban Meyer looks on during the second half the CFP National Championship college football game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images “USC is probably right behind Oregon as far as talent. Now, they don’t always play that way. “I don’t think they should move on from Riley. Keep Lincoln Riley, hire an offensive coordinator. Lincoln Riley has to go sit in defensive meetings. He’s got to go sit in special teams meetings. He’s got to quit the stupid penalties. He’s got to do the head coach things,” Meyer said. URBAN MEYER WEIGHS IN: Former national championship-winning head coach and FOX Sports analyst Urban Meyer weighed in on the future of #USC HC Lincoln Riley during an appearance on The Triple Option Show. Meyer believes USC possesses one of the most talented rosters in the Big Ten but acknowledged that the Trojans don’t consistently perform up to their potential. “USC is probably right behind Oregon as far as talent. Now, they don’t always play that way.” Despite USC’s inconsistencies, Meyer doesn’t believe the Trojans should move on from Riley. Instead, he believes Riley needs to hire an offensive coordinator and become more involved in overseeing every aspect of the program. “I don’t think they should move on from Riley. Keep Lincoln Riley, hire an offensive coordinator. Lincoln Riley has to go sit in defensive meetings. He’s got to go sit in special teams meetings. He’s got to quit the stupid penalties. He’s got to do the head coach things.” Meyer’s comments raise an interesting question surrounding the structure of USC’s coaching staff and whether Riley’s responsibilities as an offensive play-caller are limiting his effectiveness as a head coach. With a former head coach already running the defense, the change Meyer is asking for

With a former head coach already running the defense, the change Meyer is asking for comes back to the hours Riley spends building and calling the offense. Riley has said he would give up play-calling if it helped Riley told ESPN’s Paolo Uggetti at those same media days that he weighed handing off play-calling during his second year at USC and decided to keep it. “I enjoy winning a whole hell of a lot more than calling plays. The same offense scored 30 in a home win over the Ohio State Buckeyes a week after the Wisconsin loss. The other loss, 41-27 to Oregon on Sept. 26, fell more on a defense that allowed 41. USC has been flagged 70 times for 606 yards through 11 games, while its opponents have been called for 62 penalties and 498 yards. The totals lump procedural flags together with the kind Meyer called stupid, but they show USC handing back 108 more penalty yards than it has gained from opponents’ mistakes. Meyer’s argument for keeping Riley starts with the roster, which he ranks just behind Oregon’s. His remedy asks Riley to give up the one job he has kept for himself through five seasons in Los Angeles, the same job he said in July he would surrender if it helped USC win. Riley went 11-3 in his first season at USC and 24-15 over the next three. A win over UCLA would give him 44 victories in Los Angeles, and of course, the headset question will be waiting for him once USC’s season is over. item.content:encoded: Serie A Preview: Como vs Juventus – Team News, Lineups & Prediction Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia is the venue as Como and Juventus go head-to-head in a standout Serie A fixture on Sunday evening. Juventus arrive in Lombardy in improved form after recording consecutive victories across all competitions. Luis Milla scored the decisive goal at the start of the second half, securing a fourth win in five Champions League outings and keeping the Lariani firmly on course for the knockout stages. They have conceded just 10 goals, while their home form has been particularly impressive, with four victories and one draw from five matches. Another positive result would open up an eight-point gap over Juventus and strengthen their position in a fiercely contested top-four race. The Lariani also have fond recent memories of this fixture, having beaten Juventus 2-0 in both league meetings last season. They had not defeated the Turin giants at home in Serie A since 1952 before ending that long wait in October 2025. Juventus Juventus have gradually rediscovered their attacking confidence under Spalletti, winning their last two games across all competitions. After thrashing Venezia 4-0 in Serie A, the Bianconeri came from behind to defeat Omonia Nicosia 4-1 in the Europa League on Thursday. The Turin giants have now scored 14 goals in their last five outings, suggesting their attacking problems may finally be easing. However, their domestic campaign remains inconsistent, with six wins, three draws and three defeats leaving them sixth in the standings on 21 points. Juventus have also stuttered away from home, which spells trouble ahead of this showdown. They have secured only two victories from six Serie A trips this season (D2, L2), scoring eight goals and conceding the same number. Their defensive record nevertheless offers encouragement. Juventus have kept six clean sheets in 12 league games, while only Como have registered more shutouts since Spalletti took charge last November. The Bianconeri have historically dominated this fixture, winning 15 of their 30 Serie A meetings with Como. However, last season’s setbacks underline how much the balance of power has shifted, meaning they would be naive to rest on their laurels here. Team News Como remain without Moise Kean, Willy Kambwala, and Jesus Rodriguez. Maxence Caqueret also faces a race against time to recover, while Assane Diao and Jayden Addai must pass late fitness tests. Tasos Douvikas should continue to lead the attack in Kean’s absence. The Greek striker has scored 11 goals across all competitions this season and will likely receive support from Da Cunha, Nico Paz, and Martin Baturina. Juventus have several important absentees of their own. Kenan Yildiz, Khephren Thuram, and captain Manuel Locatelli remain sidelined, while Nicolás Gonzalez and Pierre Kalulu face late fitness assessments. Randal Kolo Muani and Francisco Conceicao are also expected to feature, with Douglas Luiz and Teun Koopmeiners likely to form the midfield partnership. Como vs Juventus Potential Starting Lineups Como (4-2-3-1): Butez; Couto, Chalobah, Ramon, Valle; Perrone, Milla; Da Cunha, Paz, Baturina; Douvikas. Juventus (4-2-3-1): Vicario; Celik, Bremer, Lucumi, Cabal; Douglas Luiz, Koopmeiners; Conceição, McKennie, Kolo Muani; Woltemade. Como vs Juventus Prediction Como have established themselves as one of Serie A’s most difficult teams to beat, particularly at home, and their defensive solidity should make life uncomfortable for Juventus. However, the record-time Italian champions have shown signs of improvement in recent weeks and possess enough individual quality to trouble the hosts. Both teams have been formidable defensively, so a closely contested encounter could be on the cards.

item.title: Former Georgia Star Makes Stunning Rivalry Admission Before Bulldogs Face Georgia Tech
item.description: Nov 21, 2026; Columbia, South Carolina, USA; Georgia Bulldogs quarterback Gunner Stockton (14) hands the ball off to Georgia Bulldogs running back Nate Frazier (3) during the second half against the South Carolina Gamecocks at Williams-Brice Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Blake-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) ATHENS, Ga. — Georgia football is preparing to make history against Georgia Tech on Saturday, but one former Bulldogs standout will find himself in an unusual position. His son is playing for the other team. Former Georgia running back Verron Haynes, who once delivered a memorable performance against the Yellow Jackets, will be supporting Georgia Tech as his son, Justice Haynes, attempts to upset the nation’s No. 1 team. The family connection adds another fascinating storyline to a rivalry already filled with bad blood. And this time, Georgia’s history is directly involved. Former Georgia Standout Faces Unusual Rivalry Decision Verron Haynes played for Georgia from 1999 through 2001, establishing himself as a productive running back before beginning his professional career. His most memorable performance against Georgia Tech came in 2001. Haynes rushed for 207 yards on 39 carries, helping the Bulldogs secure a victory over their in-state rivals. More than two decades later, his son is preparing to face Georgia from the opposite sideline. Justice Haynes, who previously played at Alabama and Michigan, now represents Georgia Tech. The running back also has strong family connections to Athens. Both of his parents attended Georgia, making Saturday’s matchup particularly personal. Justice Haynes Reveals Where His Father’s Loyalty Stands Despite his family’s Georgia background, Justice Haynes made it clear that his father will support him Saturday. Speaking to the Atlanta Journal-Constitution, Haynes explained that his parents have supported his football journey regardless of the program he represents. He also revealed that his father plans to wear Georgia Tech colors for the rivalry game. The admission provides an unusual twist to one of the South’s oldest college football rivalries. A former Georgia star who once helped defeat Georgia Tech will now be cheering for the Yellow Jackets. However, the decision reflects family loyalty rather than any publicly stated disagreement with Georgia. Justice has consistently emphasized the support he receives from his parents. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Blake-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) ATHENS, Ga. — Georgia football is preparing to make history against Georgia Tech on Saturday, but one former Bulldogs standout will find himself in an unusual position. His son is playing for the other team. Former Georgia running back Verron Haynes, who once delivered a memorable performance against the Yellow Jackets, will be supporting Georgia Tech as his son, Justice Haynes, attempts to upset the nation’s No. 1 team. The family connection adds another fascinating storyline to a rivalry already filled with bad blood. And this time, Georgia’s history is directly involved. Former Georgia Standout Faces Unusual Rivalry Decision Verron Haynes played for Georgia from 1999 through 2001, establishing himself as a productive running back before beginning his professional career. His most memorable performance against Georgia Tech came in 2001. Haynes rushed for 207 yards on 39 carries, helping the Bulldogs secure a victory over their in-state rivals. More than two decades later, his son is preparing to face Georgia from the opposite sideline. Justice Haynes, who previously played at Alabama and Michigan, now represents Georgia Tech. The running back also has strong family connections to Athens. Both of his parents attended Georgia, making Saturday’s matchup particularly personal. Justice Haynes Reveals Where His Father’s Loyalty Stands Despite his family’s Georgia background, Justice Haynes made it clear that his father will support him Saturday. Speaking to the Atlanta Journal-Constitution, Haynes explained that his parents have supported his football journey regardless of the program he represents. He also revealed that his father plans to wear Georgia Tech colors for the rivalry game. The admission provides an unusual twist to one of the South’s oldest college football rivalries. A former Georgia star who once helped defeat Georgia Tech will now be cheering for the Yellow Jackets. However, the decision reflects family loyalty rather than any publicly stated disagreement with Georgia. Justice has consistently emphasized the support he receives from his parents. Georgia Tech Has Opportunity to Ruin Bulldogs’ Historic Moment Saturday’s matchup carries additional significance for Georgia. The Bulldogs have defeated Georgia Tech in eight consecutive meetings, matching the longest winning streak in series history. Georgia Tech previously won eight straight games from 1949 through 1956. Now, Kirby Smart’s program has an opportunity to establish a new record with a ninth consecutive victory. However, the Yellow Jackets would love nothing more than to prevent that milestone. Georgia enters the matchup ranked No. 1 nationally with a 10-1 record. Meanwhile, Georgia Tech is 3-8 following a difficult season. The Bulldogs are favored by more than five touchdowns, according to betting lines reported by the Atlanta Journal-Constitution. Nevertheless, rivalry games can carry an emotional significance that extends beyond records and rankings. Georgia Once Recruited Justice Haynes The family connection becomes even more interesting when considering Justice Haynes’ recruiting history. Georgia recruited the running back during his high school career. However, Haynes ultimately chose Alabama before later transferring to Michigan and Georgia Tech. His journey has now brought him back to his home state, where he will face the program his father once represented. The matchup offers an opportunity to compete against one of the nation’s strongest defenses. Georgia enters Saturday allowing just 89.7 rushing yards per game. Meanwhile, Georgia Tech has relied on its running game to help offset uncertainty at quarterback. A productive performance from Haynes could help the Yellow Jackets challenge a heavily favored opponent. Kirby Smart Looks to Extend Georgia’s Dominance Georgia has controlled the rivalry throughout Smart’s tenure. The Bulldogs have won every meeting against Georgia Tech since 2017. Last season, Georgia secured a 16-9 victory in Atlanta. Now, the Bulldogs return to Sanford Stadium seeking another victory before their SEC Championship Game appearance against Texas. However, Georgia Tech has an opportunity to disrupt the Bulldogs’ momentum. The Yellow Jackets have struggled defensively throughout the season, allowing 31.5 points per game. Georgia, meanwhile, averages 41.1 points per contest. Those numbers suggest a difficult matchup for Georgia Tech. Still, the emotional stakes are considerable for both programs. A Georgia Family Will Be Wearing Different Colors For most Georgia fans, Saturday represents another opportunity to extend the Bulldogs’ dominance over their in-state rival. For the Haynes family, the afternoon carries a different meaning. Verron Haynes once helped Georgia defeat Georgia Tech with one of the most memorable rushing performances of his college career. Now, his son will attempt to help the Yellow Jackets accomplish the opposite. The former Bulldogs standout has made his priorities clear through his son’s account of the family’s support. On Saturday, he will be cheering for Justice. Even if that means wearing the colors of Georgia’s biggest in-state rival. item.title: Low turnout, BVAS glitches mar INEC mock accreditation in Ondo
item.description: By Dayo Johnson Akure The ongoing mock accreditation and voting exercise conducted by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) ahead of the 2027 general elections has recorded low voter turnout in some polling units in Ondo State, alongside technical challenges with the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS). As of the time of filing this report, findings showed that only two persons voted out of 470 registered voters at Tipper Garage, Ward 2, Unit 046. Similarly, at Champion Junction, Ward 3, Unit 15, only six voters participated in the exercise. At High Court, Ward 5, Unit 11, 11 persons were recorded as having voted out of 940 registered voters. However, the situation was different at Ajipowo, Ward 2, Unit 17, where a large turnout of voters was observed. Despite the turnout, the exercise experienced technical challenges as the BVAS reportedly failed to capture the faces of some elderly voters, causing difficulties during the accreditation process. The mock exercise is part of INEC’s preparations to test its electoral equipment and processes ahead of the 2027 general elections. The post Low turnout, BVAS glitches mar INEC mock accreditation in Ondo appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Why Tinubu should stay in office for 10 years – Akande
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Former Osun State Governor, Bisi Akande, has called for President Bola Tinubu to remain in office for 10 years, saying the period would allow him to complete ongoing projects and deliver lasting reforms. Akande made the call during an interview on the Frankly Speaking with Icon podcast, published on Friday. “He should remain in office, if possible, for another 10 years; otherwise, we go back to the situation of ‘Ebinpawa’ because there has been a foundation for hunger,” Akande said. He cited the Olubadan’s comments on road projects across the South-West, including routes linking Ijebu-Ode, Abeokuta, Oyo and Ikire, as evidence of the administration’s ongoing work. Quoting the traditional ruler, Akande said: “If you are working like this, and this had not been done 50 years before you, what again do we still say you should do, and you have not done? “But so that you will be able to complete this good job that you started, Ibadan people and Oyo State people are supporting you to do another four years.” Akande also blamed successive military administrations for what he described as decades of neglect of agriculture, education and economic development, saying their policies contributed to the country’s present difficulties. “Forty years before he came, since 1966, when the military started ruling you, you have been laying the foundation for hunger. You have abandoned your farms. You have abandoned the job. You have refused to be educated. You have refused to be modernised,” he said. He expressed optimism that Tinubu’s policies would produce significant improvements in the coming years, particularly in electricity supply and modernisation. “So in another 10 years there will be electricity everywhere. There will be modernisation,” he said. “They liberalised electricity. If you have money today, you can create electricity in your home. You can create it in your city. You can create it around you,” he said. Comparing the policy with the restrictions under previous military administrations, Akande said individuals were previously prevented from generating electricity independently. “Unlike what the military did before, if you tried to create electricity, they would arrest you. They would make you a debtor. They wouldn’t let you do it. They said only the Federal Government could do it. Tinubu came and said everybody can do it,” he added. On his own public engagements, the former governor attributed his reduced movement around the country to age, contrasting his present situation with when he was younger. The post Why Tinubu should stay in office for 10 years – Akande appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Jørgen Strand Larsen: ‘Dad and I have been best mates since I was a kid – that’s not going to change’
item.description: Striker determined to raise prostate cancer awareness after father, who scored goals for fun at amateur level in Norway, received terminal diagnosis It is a fresh Friday afternoon at Selhurst Park and, after posing for a couple of pictures in front of the red and blue Holmesdale End, Jørgen Strand Larsen holds a scarf overhead in true new-signing style. This is not the last step before a routine announcement, nor is this a run-of-the-mill club, his manicured moustache a giveaway. The Crystal Palace and Norway striker has joined forces with Prostate Cancer UK to raise awareness of the disease after his father, Atle Wester, was given a terminal diagnosis this year. Strand Larsen arrives after a recovery session following Thomas Frank’s first victory since taking charge. He devotes more than an hour to learning more about a subject close to his heart, meeting Dr Matthew Hobbs, the charity’s research director, before a round-table conversation with Mark Bright, a Palace ambassador, and a couple of fans with links to the cause. Continue reading...

item.title: Low voter turnout mars INEC mock election in Bayelsa, as accreditation process runs smoothly
item.description: •Reports across the state indicate a seamless exercise despite poor participation By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa The mock election organised by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) recorded a low voter turnout across Yenagoa, the Bayelsa State capital, on Saturday, despite reports of a smooth accreditation process. The exercise, designed to test the commission’s preparedness and assess the performance of its electoral technology ahead of the 2027 general elections, was seamless at the polling units visited. At the Kpansia Epie Community Town Hall, no fewer than nine voters had completed the accreditation process as of 11:15 a.m. when this reporter left the unit. The Assistant Presiding Officer, Sampson Wale, confirmed that operations with the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) were seamless. The story is not different at Epie II CPS Opolo II and others. The BVAS is being tested as part of efforts to identify and address possible challenges before the general elections. Though participation was relatively low, INEC officials expressed optimism that voter turnout would improve as the exercise progressed. Reports from other parts of the state also described the mock exercise as smooth. The post Low voter turnout mars INEC mock election in Bayelsa, as accreditation process runs smoothly appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2026 Kindle Paperwhite review: Page-turn buttons are back, for a price
item.description: Supply pressures, shortages, and inflation have pushed tech prices relentlessly upward over the last half-decade, and even basic gadgets haven't been immune. That's why you can spend $385 on a Raspberry Pi, or why the cheapest Amazon Kindle in 2026 costs more than the midrange one from a few years ago . "New thing, better features, same price" used to be a reliable formula, but now you're lucky if you can get the same thing for barely more than before. The 2024 Kindles all came with small price increases, but the 2026 models make them look like stellar deals. The $160 Kindle Paperwhite from two years ago wipes the floor with this year's $150 Kindle in just about every conceivable way, from screen size to front light quality to waterproofing—something to consider if you're choosing between a used or refurbished Paperwhite and one of these new models. The flagship of the now five-model-large monochrome Kindle family is the $250 2026 Paperwhite Signature Edition, which takes the core specs of the new $200 Paperwhite and puts it in a sturdy iPad-esque aluminum case instead of the typical plastic. Read full article Comments

item.description: Widow’s Bay was one of the most discussed shows of the year. Set on a small island, the series is a mix of seemingly opposing genres, following Mayor Tom Loftis (Matthew Rhys) as he tries to reshape the cursed town of Widow’s Bay into a worthwhile vacation spot. Throughout its episodes, the series straddles the line between comedy and horror, pairing hilarious workplace banter with a horrifying cursed party. It’s a show that owes equally to Parks and Rec and the mythos of Stephen King .

item.title: NPFL faces fresh scrutiny after Shooting Stars fans attack referee
item.description: The Nigeria Premier Football League (NPFL) is facing renewed scrutiny over its efforts to curb crowd violence after Shooting Stars supporters invaded the pitch and attacked match officials and Rivers United players following Friday’s 1-1 draw in Ibadan. The incident at the Lekan Salami Stadium has raised fresh concerns about the safety of players and officials in the domestic league, particularly as similar incidents have continued despite disciplinary measures imposed on offending clubs. As of Saturday, the NPFL had yet to issue an official statement on the violence. Neither Shooting Stars nor Rivers United had publicly commented on the incident. Videos circulating on social media showed supporters storming the pitch shortly after the final whistle, with one fan dressed in green striking centre referee Grema Muhammad on the head. Several Rivers United players were also reportedly attacked as the situation escalated, forcing security personnel and officers of the Nigeria Police Force to intervene and escort the match officials away from the hostile crowd. In another video from the incident, Rivers United players were seen assisting an injured match official. The violence overshadowed the encounter, which ended in a 1-1 draw, with both teams sharing the points. The latest incident has also revived concerns about previous cases of supporter violence at the Ibadan stadium. On April 6, 2025, Shooting Stars supporters reportedly attacked members of the Ikorodu City delegation and match officials following a goalless draw between the two sides. The incident also involved damage to Ikorodu City’s team bus. The attack comes amid a series of disciplinary actions by the NPFL against clubs over security breaches and misconduct during the ongoing 2026/27 season. The repeated incidents have raised questions about the effectiveness of the league’s disciplinary measures in preventing violence at match venues. Although the NPFL has previously imposed financial penalties, points deductions and stadium restrictions on clubs over security breaches, Friday’s attack in Ibadan represents another test of its efforts to protect players, match officials and other participants. The league is expected to review available video footage and match reports before deciding whether to open disciplinary proceedings against Shooting Stars. The post NPFL faces fresh scrutiny after Shooting Stars fans attack referee appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Gunmen kill 51-year-old man, two others in fresh Plateau attack
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Gunmen have killed three persons in a fresh attack on Nkiedowro community in Teegbe District of Bassa Local Government Area of Plateau State, throwing residents into mourning. The attack, which occurred on Friday night, claimed the lives of three Irigwe natives, bringing to 20 the number of Irigwe people reportedly killed within the week, according to the National Publicity Secretary of the Irigwe Youth Movement, Joseph Chudu Yonkpa. Yonkpa, who confirmed the killings in a statement made available to newsmen on Saturday, said the attackers launched two separate ambushes on the community. “Yesterday night, Fulani militias launched two separate ambushes at Nkiedowro, Teegbe District, killing three Irigwe natives,” he said. He identified the victims as Ngudo Kura, 51; Hosea Ishaya, 26; and Naomi Izeh, 22. “This makes it a total of 20 Irigwe people killed this week in an unprovoked manner,” Yonkpa added. He expressed condolences to the families of the victims and the entire Irigwe community, praying for the repose of the souls of the deceased. Our correspondent reports that the latest killings occurred barely two days after 17 persons were given a mass burial following an attack on the Tafi Gana community, also in Bassa Local Government Area. The development has heightened concerns over the security situation in the area, with residents reportedly apprehensive about possible further attacks. The Irigwe Youth Movement urged residents to remain vigilant and avoid movements that could expose them to danger. “We call on our people to intensify vigilance, avoid late-night and isolated movements, and report suspicious movements to the relevant authorities,” Yonkpa said. The group also appealed to security agencies to strengthen surveillance and take necessary measures to protect communities in the area. Efforts to get the reaction of security operatives were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. The post Gunmen kill 51-year-old man, two others in fresh Plateau attack appeared first on Vanguard News .

He identified the victims as Ngudo Kura, 51; Hosea Ishaya, 26; and Naomi Izeh, 22. “This makes it a total of 20 Irigwe people killed this week in an unprovoked manner,” Yonkpa added. He expressed condolences to the families of the victims and the entire Irigwe community, praying for the repose of the souls of the deceased. Our correspondent reports that the latest killings occurred barely two days after 17 persons were given a mass burial following an attack on the Tafi Gana community, also in Bassa Local Government Area. The development has heightened concerns over the security situation in the area, with residents reportedly apprehensive about possible further attacks. The Irigwe Youth Movement urged residents to remain vigilant and avoid movements that could expose them to danger. “We call on our people to intensify vigilance, avoid late-night and isolated movements, and report suspicious movements to the relevant authorities,” Yonkpa said. The group also appealed to security agencies to strengthen surveillance and take necessary measures to protect communities in the area. Efforts to get the reaction of security operatives were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. The post Gunmen kill 51-year-old man, two others in fresh Plateau attack appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: INEC Declares Readiness For 2027, Expresses Satisfaction With Plateau Mock Election
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has declared its readiness for the 2027 general elections, assuring Nigerians that it is committed to conducting free, inclusive, credible and transparent polls. INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, gave the assurance while monitoring Saturday’s mock election in Plateau State, where he expressed satisfaction with the turnout of voters and the conduct of the exercise. Amupitan said the mock election was designed to test the functionality of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV), as well as assess the efficiency of the accreditation process ahead of the 2027 general elections. INEC Chairman Amupitan inspecting the exercise in Jos on Saturday, November 28, 2026. He commended voters for their orderly conduct, expressing delight at seeing an elderly woman turn out for the exercise and successfully undergo accreditation. “You can see yourself that the turnout is very good. What we are trying to test is actually the working of the machines, which are the BVAS and the IReV, and voters are being accredited. You can see how orderly it is going. From what we have seen, I am impressed,” he said. The INEC chairman acknowledged the support of the Plateau State Independent Electoral Commission in mobilising residents for the exercise but noted that the environmental sanitation exercise earlier scheduled for Saturday may have affected early participation, as some residents had indicated they would be unable to come out in time. On the commission’s preparedness for the 2027 elections, Amupitan said INEC was determined to deliver one of the best elections in the country’s history. “For the 2027 general elections, INEC is prepared, and I want to assure all Nigerians that we are going to have one of the best elections. We are determined that the 2027 election will be free, inclusive, credible and transparent,” he stated. Addressing concerns over the security situation in the country, the INEC chairman said the commission was working with relevant security agencies to ensure the protection of voters and electoral personnel during the forthcoming elections. He disclosed that INEC recently convened a one-day national security conference where stakeholders deliberated on security challenges and measures to safeguard the electoral process. INEC Chairman, Joash Amupitan, seen addressing staff and voters in Jos on Saturday, NOVEMBER 28, 2026. Amupitan further revealed that the commission had conducted a risk assessment of polling units across the country, with identified locations shared with law enforcement agencies to enable them to strengthen security arrangements ahead of the elections. “We have done what we call a risk assessment of all the polling units in Nigeria, and we have identified all the polling units and shared them with the law enforcement agencies so that they can make extra preparations ahead of the elections,” he said. item.title: Omo-Agege attack: How I learned of my husband’s death – Wife of slain NDC member
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Gift Umokoro, wife of slain Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) member Comrade Efemena Umokoro, has recounted how she learnt of her husband’s death following an attack on party members in Ughelli, Delta State. In an interview with BBC News Pidgin, Gift said she initially became suspicious after receiving calls from her husband’s friend and relatives, who asked whether she had heard from him without telling her what had happened. She said her husband’s friend first called to ask where she was before requesting that she contact her husband because she wanted to speak with him. “I was surprised and I asked her why she could not call my husband herself if she indeed wanted to talk to him,” Gift said. She explained that the situation became more suspicious when her husband’s aunt later called to ask whether she had heard from him. Her sister also called with the same question. Gift said she subsequently checked social media and began seeing RIP messages but found it difficult to believe that her husband was dead. “I did not know how he ended up in Ughelli because it was Abraka he told me he was going to,” she said. Recounting her husband’s last movements, Gift said he left home that morning wearing a white jalabia, explaining that he wanted to visit a political party member and one of the House of Assembly members. She said their last conversation was around 3:30pm. Gift further disclosed that when she contacted her husband’s friends, they initially denied that he had died, telling her instead that he had sustained injuries and was receiving treatment at a hospital. She said she waited for them to come and take her to see him, but nobody showed up that evening. “The next morning, they told me they were with him in the hospital. I waited from 6am till whenever. When I noticed nobody was coming, that was when I knew something was up,” she recounted. Describing her late husband as a devoted father, Gift said he was deeply committed to his children and appealed to authorities to ensure that those responsible for his killing were brought to justice. “He does not joke with his children. He should get justice. They should find the people that killed him,” she said. Comrade Umokoro was among the NDC members killed during an attack on party supporters in Ughelli, Delta State, during a political gathering involving former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege. The post Omo-Agege attack: How I learned of my husband’s death – Wife of slain NDC member appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Numbers ‘Impressive’ As Voters Turnout For INEC Mock Exercise In Kano
item.description: The mock accreditation for the 2027 general elections is underway in Paniso ward, Kano, as voters were seen turning out in seemingly impressive numbers for the exercise, compared to other regions in the country. Our correspondent, who monitored one of the selected polling units, noted that two INEC staff and two ad hoc personnel are testing the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices. Although voter turnout is still relatively low as against what is expected, the exercise is progressing smoothly, with no discrepancies reported and the BVAS thumbprint verification functioning as expected so far. Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Joash Amupitan, is currently in Jos to inspect the ongoing mock accreditation exercise, ahead of the 2027 general elections. It’s about seven weeks before the 2027 general election, and INEC is today running a nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise in all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). Professor Joash Amupitan, INEC Chairman, disclosed this at the INEC and Office of the National Security Adviser ONSA) Strategic Election Security Conference in Abuja on Thursday. According to him, the exercise would put the Commission’s new equipment and result systems under live conditions. “While this exercise allows INEC to stress-test our upgraded BVAS devices and verify our stricter INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) validation safeguards—which automatically block arithmetic inconsistencies and over-voting, it also serves as an essential live dry run for our security architecture,” he said. The presidential and National Assembly elections hold on 16 January 2027 across 177,299 polling units, with governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections to follow on 6 February 2027. The post Numbers ‘Impressive’ As Voters Turnout For INEC Mock Exercise In Kano appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: 12 grains of dust found high in Earth's atmosphere reveal secrets of water at the edge of the solar system
item.description: A dozen grains of dust that have wandered in from the distant Kuiper Belt beyond Neptune were found floating in Earth's stratosphere. And it turns out they hold the secrets of a special kind of 'heavy' water that seems to be surprisingly abundant in the outer solar system. When analyzed by a team of scientists the 12 dust grains, which were captured by NASA's stratospheric ER-2 research aircraft, show signs of having interacted with a form of water that contains heavy oxygen isotopes. This is important because to better understand how the planets formed, scientists are seeking to understand how various materials were distributed around the early solar system 4.5 billion years ago. If there is a reservoir of heavy water out in the solar system's hinterlands, understanding how that water got out there and stayed out there will inform models that describe the growth of the planets. Water consists of two hydrogen atoms and an oxygen atom. What we usually refer to as heavy water is water that contains a heavy isotope of hydrogen. An isotope is an atom that contains the usual number of protons for that element, but a different number of neutrons . Elements are determined by the number of protons they contain. For example, hydrogen always has just one proton. Ordinary 'light' hydrogen has 1 proton and no neutrons, but its heavy isotopes – deuterium and tritium – contain 1 and 2 neutrons, respectively, in addition to the proton. However, there's another kind of water that features heavy isotopes of oxygen instead. Ordinary 'light' oxygen is made from 8 protons and 8 neutrons and is hence known as oxygen-16 but some oxygen isotopes can have 9 or 10 neutrons, and we call these isotopes oxygen-17 or -18. There have been a few clues that such a reservoir exists. Mineralogical evidence from a single carbonaceous chondritic meteorite and measurements from comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko indicated the presence of minerals that had formed from interactions between silicate rock and abundant oxygen-heavy variety of water, but it was not clear whether these were isolated instances or a clue to something more widespread. An illustration comparing the locations of the solar system planets to the Kuiper Belt and the Oort Cloud, a theorized shell of icy objects at the farthest reaches of our solar system. (Image credit: ESA) Another data point comes from NASA's Genesis mission, which launched in 2001 and collected particles from the solar wind that were subsequently returned to Earth for study. The analysis of these particles indicated that the sun contains proportionally more ordinary 'light' oxygen than Earth and most meteorites. This suggests that there could be an outwards gradient of increasing abundance of heavy oxygen. Yet the Kuiper Belt is so far away that it makes finding more evidence for this difficult. However, rather than having to go to the Kuiper Belt to sample the water-ice there, dust grains can bring a little bit of the Kuiper Belt to us. T
item.dc:creator: Keith Cooper
item.content:encoded: A dozen grains of dust that have wandered in from the distant Kuiper Belt beyond Neptune were found floating in Earth's stratosphere. And it turns out they hold the secrets of a special kind of 'heavy' water that seems to be surprisingly abundant in the outer solar system. When analyzed by a team of scientists the 12 dust grains, which were captured by NASA's stratospheric ER-2 research aircraft, show signs of having interacted with a form of water that contains heavy oxygen isotopes. This is important because to better understand how the planets formed, scientists are seeking to understand how various materials were distributed around the early solar system 4.5 billion years ago. If there is a reservoir of heavy water out in the solar system's hinterlands, understanding how that water got out there and stayed out there will inform models that describe the growth of the planets. Water consists of two hydrogen atoms and an oxygen atom. What we usually refer to as heavy water is water that contains a heavy isotope of hydrogen. An isotope is an atom that contains the usual number of protons for that element, but a different number of neutrons . Elements are determined by the number of protons they contain. For example, hydrogen always has just one proton. Ordinary 'light' hydrogen has 1 proton and no neutrons, but its heavy isotopes – deuterium and tritium – contain 1 and 2 neutrons, respectively, in addition to the proton. However, there's another kind of water that features heavy isotopes of oxygen instead. Ordinary 'light' oxygen is made from 8 protons and 8 neutrons and is hence known as oxygen-16 but some oxygen isotopes can have 9 or 10 neutrons, and we call these isotopes oxygen-17 or -18. There have been a few clues that such a reservoir exists. Mineralogical evidence from a single carbonaceous chondritic meteorite and measurements from comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko indicated the presence of minerals that had formed from interactions between silicate rock and abundant oxygen-heavy variety of water, but it was not clear whether these were isolated instances or a clue to something more widespread. An illustration comparing the locations of the solar system planets to the Kuiper Belt and the Oort Cloud, a theorized shell of icy objects at the farthest reaches of our solar system. (Image credit: ESA) Another data point comes from NASA's Genesis mission, which launched in 2001 and collected particles from the solar wind that were subsequently returned to Earth for study. The analysis of these particles indicated that the sun contains proportionally more ordinary 'light' oxygen than Earth and most meteorites. This suggests that there could be an outwards gradient of increasing abundance of heavy oxygen. Yet the Kuiper Belt is so far away that it makes finding more evidence for this difficult. However, rather than having to go to the Kuiper Belt to sample the water-ice there, dust grains can bring a little bit of the Kuiper Belt to us. Those 12 dust grains all started out in the Kuiper Belt, but a phenomenon known as Poynting–Robertson drag, whereby dust particles absorb heat coming from the sun and then re-radiate it as thermal infrared in all directions, which slows the dust particles down and causes their orbit to drift in towards the sun. Those particular 12 dust grains got lucky – they were intercepted by Earth and their small size, mass and velocity meant they survived entry into the atmosphere. If the ER-2 aircraft hadn't picked them up, they may well have drifted down to the ground. One of two NASA operated ER-2 high-altitude research planes. (Image credit: NASA/Carla Thomas) A team of scientists led by NASA's Lindsay Keller's team used advanced electron microscopy at the agency's Johnson Space Center, and then the ion microprobe at the University of California, Los Angeles, to study the hydrated minerals inside the tiny dust grains that are smaller than a millimeter across. The grains were identified as having come from the Kuiper Belt by the pattern of tracks, or scars, left in them by energetic particles from the sun – an identifying characteristic of Kuiper Belt dust. Thanks to these instruments, Keller's team spotted hydrated clay minerals that formed when water infused with heavy oxygen interacted with silicate minerals enriched with iron-nickel and sulfide in cold temperatures. These dust grains formed 4.5 billion years ago, when the planets were being assembled from material in a circumstellar disk of gas and dust around the young sun. According to their models, Keller's team were able to place an upper limit on how much heavy oxygen water there is in the Kuiper Belt, calculating a 15% greater ratio of oxygen-18 to oxygen-16 than is found in Earth's oceans. Scanning transmission electron microscope images of some of the dust grains, showing various facets of their mineralogy. (Image credit: Keller et al/Science Advances 2026) What makes this discovery even more intriguing is that there seems to be a cut-off somewhere between the inner solar system and the Kuiper Belt. Lots of material in the planet-forming disk was well mixed together, and we can see this in the compositions of meteorites that originate from various sources. However, most meteorites do not contain much heavy oxygen. Something must have blocked the heavy oxygen from moving inwards and becoming part of planetary bodies closer to the sun. "The limited mixing between these outer solar system reservoirs suggests that the heavy water reservoir in the outer solar system was isolated from the inner regions, most likely by Saturn or in combination with the ice giants," write Keller's team in their research paper. This further illustrates the complexity of the chemistry within the planet-forming disk that formed the solar system, including Earth. When seeking to understand the development of the solar system's chemistry, we must also factor in the planets themselves and the role they played in directing that chemistry, resulting in the solar system that we see today. The analysis of the dust grains was published on Nov. 11 in the journal Science Advances

item.title: Kano varsity bans students, lecturers from exchanging gifts
item.description: Northwest University, Kano, has prohibited students and lecturers from giving or receiving gifts in connection with university services, warning that anyone who violates the directive will face disciplinary action. The university classified the practice as corruption and serious misconduct, stressing that the ban applies to both staff and students, irrespective of the intentions behind the gifts. The Registrar, Isyaku Adamu, announced the directive in a statement issued on Friday, following public attention generated by reports of students presenting gifts to lecturers recognised as the best level coordinators or lecturers in their respective categories. According to the registrar, the practice could damage the institution’s reputation and violate provisions of its Service Conditions and Regulations (2025), as amended. The university specifically identified the giving and receiving of gifts as acts of corruption and conduct capable of bringing the institution into disrepute. “Consequently, any staff or students found involved in giving and/or receiving gift items for university services rendered will be charged with committing an act(s) of serious misconduct and the university will immediately initiate disciplinary process against the staff or students according to the university’s regulations,” Adamu said. He added that offenders would be liable to sanctions under Section 16 of the regulations. The registrar consequently urged members of the university community to observe the institution’s rules, ethical standards and best practices to avoid disciplinary action. He also called on staff and students to take the directive seriously, adding, “A stitch in time saves nine!” Northwest University, Kano, is a state-owned institution established by the Kano State Government in 2012. It was renamed Yusuf Maitama Sule University in 2017 before reverting to its original name in 2024 following an amendment to the state law establishing it. The post Kano varsity bans students, lecturers from exchanging gifts appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: DWP cyber incident ‘probably an attack’, says former UK chief technology officer
item.description: Government took down pensions and benefits portal on Thursday but said regular payments will not be affected A serious cyber incident that forced ministers to take down online benefits and pension services was “probably an attack”, the UK’s former chief technology officer has said. The Department for Work and Pensions took down several systems that appeared to still be offline on Saturday morning. David Knott, who led government technology until December 2025, said much infrastructure was outdated, and underinvestment in defence and increasing sophistication of attacks meant it was only getting more vulnerable. item.title: [Full list]Super Falcons arrivals rise to 18 ahead of Algeria friendlies
item.description: Eighteen Super Falcons players have arrived in camp ahead of Nigeria’s international friendly against Algeria, scheduled for November 30. The Super Falcons officials confirmed the development in a squad update on X featuring the names of the players who have reported to camp. The arrivals include Super Falcons captain Asisat Oshoala, goalkeeper Chiamaka Nnadozie, defender Michelle Alozie and midfielder Jennifer Echegini. Other players who have arrived are Shukurat Oladipo, Regina Otu, Folashade Ijamilusi, Olamide Adugbe, Christiana Uzoma, Glory Ogbonna, Suliat Abideen, Glory Edet, Valentina Uroko, Joy Igbokwe, Fatimoh Solaty, Blessing Nkor, Comfort Erhabor and Nicole Payne. The Falcons are preparing for the encounter against Algeria, which is scheduled to kick off at 6pm on November 30. The 18 players represent the arrivals so far from the 23 player squad, with the remaining players expected to join the team in camp. Full list of players who have arrived Shukurat Oladipo Regina Otu Folashade Ijamilusi Olamide Adugbe Christiana Uzoma Glory Ogbonna Suliat Abideen Chiamaka Nnadozi Michelle Alozie Glory Edet Valentina Uroko Joy Igbokwe Fatimoh Solaty Blessing Nkor Comfort Erhabor Asisat Oshoala Nicole Payne Jennifer Echegini The camp still awaits the arrival of Oluwatosin Demehin, Christy Ucheibe, Shakirat Moshood, Blessing Okpe, Joy Omewa and Toni Payne. item.title: UEFA begins probe into Marseille, Besiktas fans clash
item.description: UEFA has opened disciplinary investigations into violent incidents involving supporters of Marseille and Besiktas during their respective Europa League fixtures on Thursday. The European football governing body announced the probes on Friday, following clashes between Marseille and Levski Sofia supporters in France and a confrontation between Besiktas fans and police in Georgia. In Marseille, several hundred home supporters confronted visiting Levski Sofia fans, leaving five Bulgarian supporters hospitalised. French magistrates have also launched an investigation into alleged intentional violence involving some Marseille supporters. Authorities are equally examining allegations of incitement to hatred following claims of Nazi salutes and provocations by Bulgarian fans. Meanwhile, Besiktas’ encounter with Israeli side Hapoel Beer-Sheva in Batumi, Georgia, was temporarily halted after clashes broke out between supporters and police. The incident followed the display of a pro-Palestinian banner bearing the inscription, “Revolt against the occupation, freedom for Palestine”, alongside Palestinian flags and chants against Israel. UEFA said the incidents contradicted its commitment to ensuring that football matches are played in an atmosphere of peace, mutual respect and sporting fairness. “The events witnessed at the above-mentioned matches run counter… to UEFA’s objective, enshrined in its Statutes, of ensuring that football matches are played in a spirit of peace, mutual respect and sporting fairness,” the governing body said. It added that it had appointed Ethics and Disciplinary Inspectors to investigate the incidents. The Besiktas fixture was moved from Istanbul to Georgia after Turkish authorities informed UEFA that the match could not be hosted in Turkey for safety and security reasons. The relocation came amid worsening diplomatic relations between Turkey and Israel following the outbreak of the Gaza war. The post UEFA begins probe into Marseille, Besiktas fans clash appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Security, INEC’s Presence Seen As Voters Trickle To Polling Units In Imo
item.description: Despite the presence of security officers and staff members of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), seen at Polling 08013 Azuzi 4 Uzi Primary School, with registered voters of 803, no single voter for mock accreditation is yet to be seen as of 11:40 am. Onuoha Onyewuchi at Azuzi Ward 4, Uzi Primary School. Onuoha Onyewuchi at Azuzi Ward 4, Uzi Primary School complained of discrepancies in the polling units. “Actually, some of us here, our various polling units; I don’t think they have been able to bring it down here. What they told us here is that there are 001-013. Some of us, 008, 005, in fact, numerous units are not here. “So, it’s only these two people that are here with me. We are still waiting for them.” Some women were also seen loitering and unable to get accredited. While briefing the media, Professor Joash Amupitan, INEC Chairman, at the INEC and Office of the National Security Adviser ONSA) Strategic Election Security Conference in Abuja on Thursday, said the exercise would put the Commission’s new equipment and result systems under live conditions. “While this exercise allows INEC to stress-test our upgraded BVAS devices and verify our stricter INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) validation safeguards—which automatically block arithmetic inconsistencies and over-voting- it also serves as an essential live dry run for our security architecture,” he said. Ihetiobi Christian Uche, the INEC Assistant Electoral Officer, Operations, Ngorokpala LGA, speaking to Channels Television on the Mock accreditation election at Umuowa Ward 6 polling unit 006, Ngorokpala LGA, said officials arrived since 8:30 am, but no one has come for accreditation. According to him, people come only to make inquiries about PVC collection, alleging that INEC did not carry out enough sensitisation. The post Security, INEC’s Presence Seen As Voters Trickle To Polling Units In Imo appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: World Health Organization sounds alarm as measles fight stalls
item.description: Global measles deaths hit a historic low in 2025, the World Health Organization said on Friday, although millions of children ⁠still missed vaccinations and outbreaks persisted in dozens of countries. The UN health agency estimated 9.8 million measles cases and about 72,000 deaths worldwide in 2025 — down 74% from 37.8 million cases in 2000, with deaths falling roughly 91% from about 769,000.

item.title: INEC’s Mock Accreditation Begins In Lagos
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) mock accreditation has begun in Lagos State as voters are seen being attended to by staff of the Commission. The REC is expected at the Ward K PU 002 anytime soon at the All Saints Anglican Primary School, Yaba. So far, the exercise has gone smoothly with average accreditation and voting time put at 1-2 minutes. There is police presence, monitors from YIAGA, Party representatives, and other stakeholders. It’s about seven weeks before the 2027 general election, and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) will today run a nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise in all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). While briefing the media, Professor Joash Amupitan, INEC Chairman, at the INEC and Office of the National Security Adviser ONSA) Strategic Election Security Conference in Abuja on Thursday, said the exercise would put the Commission’s new equipment and result systems under live conditions. “While this exercise allows INEC to stress-test our upgraded BVAS devices and verify our stricter INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) validation safeguards—which automatically block arithmetic inconsistencies and over-voting- it also serves as an essential live dry run for our security architecture,” he said. The post INEC’s Mock Accreditation Begins In Lagos appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: 30 Years Later, Star Trek's Greatest 'Next Generation' Movie Is Officially Free to Stream
item.description: Turning a successful television series into a movie isn't as easy as just giving the cast a bigger budget and adding in more explosions. What works on the small screen doesn't always translate to theaters, especially when filmmakers lose sight of what made audiences fall in love with the characters in the first place. Fortunately, Star Trek : First Contact understood that bigger could be better, provided the spectacle didn't come at the expense of the characters.

item.title: UK court jails Nigerian man for beating wife, faces deportation
item.description: A 44-year-old Nigerian man, John Onyejiaka, has been jailed for 23 months in the United Kingdom for strangling and assaulting his wife during a domestic dispute. Onyejiaka, who pleaded guilty to strangulation, was sentenced at Stoke-on-Trent Crown Court and handed an eight-year restraining order barring him from approaching or contacting the victim. He is also expected to be deported to Nigeria after serving his sentence, following the expiration of his UK visa in November last year. According to The Sentinel, prosecutor Emily Andrew told the court that Onyejiaka and his wife moved from Nigeria to the UK in 2024 and had experienced difficulties in their marriage. The court heard that the couple argued on January 9, after which the woman left their home in Norton, Staffordshire, to stay with a friend. When she returned two days later, Onyejiaka asked her to go into their bedroom. Andrew said the woman agreed, but her response angered Onyejiaka, who then attacked her. “He stood in front of her and towered over her with a clenched fist. She screamed. He grabbed her jumper. He hit her to the face and head. He shouted, ‘I am going to kill you’, while hitting her,” the prosecutor told the court. The prosecutor further said the victim fell to the floor and attempted to crawl out of the room, but Onyejiaka stopped her. In a victim impact statement, she said the attack had left her with flashbacks and made her more anxious. “It has had a lasting impact on me. I am doing my best to move forward but it has affected how I feel on a day-to-day basis,” she said. Defence counsel Elizabeth Power told the court that Onyejiaka was remorseful and had worked as a carer, warehouse employee and, most recently, a delivery driver for DPD. She said he had received a 60-day notice to leave the UK on December 10 last year and wanted to return to Nigeria, where his mother and siblings live. Sentencing him, Recorder Jeremy Robson described the incident as a sustained attack on a woman who was effectively trapped. “You struck her multiple times. She tried to get out through a window. You stopped her, banged her head against a wall and squeezed her around the neck,” he said. The judge added that Onyejiaka had prevented his wife from leaving the room and seeking assistance, deliberately taking her to an isolated place. He also noted that Onyejiaka’s visa had expired in November last year and that the defendant accepted he would be deported to Nigeria following the proceedings. The post UK court jails Nigerian man for beating wife, faces deportation appeared first on Vanguard News .
